title: Smashburger Meetup – A Sunny-Day Burger & Milkshake Social in the Galleria
description: This lively Smashburger gathering in the Galleria brought together great weather, good company, and nostalgic comfort food—all the makings of a fun, relaxed mid-April outing. With clear skies overhead, it was the perfect day for burgers, fries, milkshakes, and conversation.Smashburger has long dotted Houston’s food scene, but this event offered a great excuse to revisit the familiar chain in a social setting. While many attendees opted for burgers, the grilled chicken sandwich held its own—hot,
author: Sara Loren
html:
This lively Smashburger gathering in the Galleria brought together great weather, good company, and nostalgic comfort food—all the makings of a fun, relaxed mid-April outing. With clear skies overhead, it was the perfect day for burgers, fries, milkshakes, and conversation.


Smashburger has long dotted Houston’s food scene, but this event offered a great excuse to revisit the familiar chain in a social setting. While many attendees opted for burgers, the grilled chicken sandwich held its own—hot, fresh, and served on toasted buns with crisp tomato slices. Though the avocado add-on fell flat (prepackaged in flavor and initially forgotten), the rest of the meal delivered warm satisfaction. The rosemary-dusted tater tots were a standout: crispy, aromatic, and wonderfully seasoned. And the strawberry milkshake? Pure childhood nostalgia in a cup—creamy, sweet, and perfectly paired with a savory plate.


Surrounded by friendly faces and sunny weather, the meetup was a delightful reminder of how simple comfort foods can bring people together.


Event Highlights:

  • Grilled chicken sandwich (simple, fresh & toasted buns)

  • Crispy rosemary tater tots

  • Sweet, creamy strawberry milkshake

  • Warm spring weather & friendly conversation

  • A central Galleria location, easy to revisit


Review

Sara I. (Apr 20, 2023):

“What a wonderful foodtastic event! Clear and sunny skies called for a milkshake paired with burgers and fries. Smashburger has been around for some time... scattered throughout Houston, but I had barely visited in the past. Simply because I don't eat burgers that often. But are they tasty? Most definitely. Whether stacked, smashed or simply a classic patty no cheese, you can't go wrong.


I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich. Paired it with tator tots and a strawberry milkshake. No frills, just simple. Asked for avocado with my sandwich as well. Meal came out piping hot and fresh. The grilled chicken breast was on the smaller side, but still good. Buns were toasted and the tomato slices were fresh in the sandwich. The only thing that was missing was the avocado — they forgot to put it in the meal so I had to go and grab it. Avocado was a let down because it tasted dull and prepackaged, just as similar as the ones from Sam's club.

Other than that, my meal was good. Fresh rosemary tossed into crispy and warm tator tots? Goood stuff! As well as the sweet and creamy strawberry milkshake paired with the meal. Very nostalgic of childhood.


Met with others as we chowed down on good grub. Twas warm and friendly company on that bright day. Will I revisit this particular Smashburger location? Most definitely. It's central within most spots in the inner loop.

Until next time!”



Category: Food Events, Casual Dining Meetups 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston 


Tags: Smashburger Houston event, Galleria burger spots, milkshake social Houston, casual dining meetups, tater tots Houston, grilled chicken sandwich review

author: Sara Loren
html:
Step into the cozy, quick-stop charm of Tim Hortons in Stafford—a compact corner café near Meadows Place that delivers big on seasonal flavor. Though the interior is small and snug, the drive-thru keeps things moving with quick, efficient service and friendly staff. This is classic commercial coffee done right: reliable, flavorful, and refreshingly unpretentious.


October brings out the magic here. From pumpkin spice delights to their fun, festive Reese’s Peanut Butter collaboration drinks, Tim Hortons leans fully into spooky-season joy. Their Halloween TimBits buckets are a treat for both kids and adults, and the selection of pastries—from the crisp spinach artichoke puff to their beloved honey donut—never disappoint. Whether you’re craving a refreshing iced mocha or a creamy hot latte, this spot makes for an easy, satisfying grab-and-go stop on your way into the city.


Must-Try Items:

  • Halloween TimBits Bucket

  • Reese’s PB seasonal drinks

  • Pumpkin Spice lattes and coffees

  • Iced Mocha

Reviews

 Sara I. (Oct 7, 2025):

 “Halloween spooky flavors are here.. such as their collab with anything Reeses PB flavors and all things autumnal pumpkin spice. They also have Halloween TimBits buckets for all things trick or treat. Oh my, I am loving it and Tim Hortons has always been a favorite grab and go coffee spot for me. This location is a bit small and cramped, tucked into a little corner near meadows place. It is definitely a smaller location but I typically visit their drive thru. Their service is quick and efficient, no complaints. Coffee is good, products are good.. there's nothing else to say. Its commercial coffee given with prompt service. We will probably revisit and grab a timbits halloween bucket when given a chance! Until next time. xoxo ~”

title: Kolache Shoppe – Greenway’s Cozy Grab-and-Go Breakfast Haven
description: Kolache Shoppe in Greenway is the definition of a warm, comforting morning stop—tucked quietly into a cozy corner of Houston’s inner loop. This small but inviting bakery is perfect for those early hours when you need something fresh, quick, and reliably satisfying. With a closing time of 12 pm sharp, it’s the kind of place you want to get to early, especially before your favorite kolaches sell out.The menu offers a solid mix of classic meat-filled kolaches, vegetarian options, and beloved staple
author: Sara Loren
html:
Kolache Shoppe in Greenway is the definition of a warm, comforting morning stop—tucked quietly into a cozy corner of Houston’s inner loop. This small but inviting bakery is perfect for those early hours when you need something fresh, quick, and reliably satisfying. With a closing time of 12 pm sharp, it’s the kind of place you want to get to early, especially before your favorite kolaches sell out.


The menu offers a solid mix of classic meat-filled kolaches, vegetarian options, and beloved staples like egg-and-cheese, which is a hit even with little ones. Each kolache is tender, fluffy, and generously filled—simple, delicious fuel for busy mornings. Pair your pick with a cup of their hot coffee, and you’ve got the makings of a cozy, grab-and-go breakfast moment.


While the shop itself is small and leans more toward takeout, there are a few outdoor tables available for a quick sit-down. Service is consistently friendly, and the kolaches are always warm and fresh, making it a reliable neighborhood favorite. Dessert kolaches are on the menu too—perfect for a future visit if you’ve got a sweet tooth waiting to be indulged.


Must-Try Items:

  • Egg & Cheese Kolache

  • Brisket Kolache

  • Vegetarian Kolache options

  • Hot Coffee

  • Dessert Kolaches (for next time!)


Reviews

Sara I. (Sep 13, 2025):

 “Tucked in a cozy corner on Greenway... Kolache Shoppe is a nice option for a quick and warm breakfast experience. They close at 12pm, so get there before then!! Good options for kolaches.. plenty of vegetarian and regular meat options such as brisket kolaches and a few other ones. My son loves their egg and cheese kolache and it makes for a perfect grab and go meal every once in awhile. Greenway is a busy area within the inner loop of Houston, so this is as good as it gets for decent and fresh kolaches. They are tender and full of the good stuff. Don't arrive too late as they might run out of your favorite. Kolache Shoppe serves up hot coffee as well so pair it with your order! These are what cozy morning moments are made of. This spot isn't that big...so as mentioned, it's more of a grab and go spot. They have exterior seating outside, but it's limited with just a few tables and chairs. We have visited a few times over the year and have experienced friendly service and warm, fresh items. I have not tried any of their dessert kolaches.. which is a surprise since I have a sweet tooth, but definitely next time. All the fluff and all the good stuff, try it for yourself! This is a nice spot to visit and venture off to your weekend hangouts or errands!”


Category: Bakeries, Czech, Breakfast & Brunch 

Location: Greenway, Houston

html:
WEST on WEST—affectionately known as WoW—has quickly transformed from an empty lot into one of Westchase’s most vibrant up-and-coming shopping plazas. What was once a quiet patch of land in 2023 is now a lively hub filling up with boutiques, cafés, playful attractions, and bright, nostalgic energy. It’s the kind of place that keeps evolving, making each visit a little different from the last.


With new shops popping up regularly and colorful, family-friendly stops like TESO Life bringing 90s-inspired fun, WoW is becoming a weekend stroll favorite. Claw machines glow with neon charm, Sanrio characters make surprise appearances, and there’s a sense of joyful exploration woven into the experience. Whether you're running errands, meeting a friend, or simply wandering, this plaza delivers a cheerful dose of nostalgia and discovery.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Vibrant mix of boutiques, cafés, and specialty shops

  • TESO Life with fun 90s-style claw machines

  • Family-friendly atmosphere with kid-approved activities

  • A still-growing plaza worth revisiting as new vendors move in


Review

Sara I. (Aug 30, 2025): 

“I remember when Mark pointed out WoW plaza back in 2023... it was an empty lot. We were hanging out that day, running on some Trader Joe's errands. Lol.


Fast forward and I have had the chance to visit WoW twice so far... earlier in the year and this week.

It was fun.


The plaza continues to fill up with shoppes, boutiques and cafes. I visited TESO Life earlier in the year and brought back bébé with me. He loved the bright claw machines which have been all the rage this summer season. Hello 90's vibrancy and excitement. No Labubu for us, we're good. We were happy to hang out with Pekkle the duck instead... Sanrio for life. Again… cue the 90s vibes. Thank you for joining in on the adventure this week.... Both Mark and I are 16 years Yelp Elite... And it's always fun to chat about the city and the latest scoop of what goes on in town.


Looking forward to revisiting WoW - West on West, when more shops open and pop up!”

Nestled within the vibrant neighborhood of Tanglewood and connected to a serene apartment community, this café blends convenience with comfort. Among all Common Bond locations across Houston, this one stands out as a favorite for its inviting design, calm environment, and consistently friendly service.


Hues of blue, pink, and yellow light up the décor, creating a cozy space perfect for catching up with friends, reading, or getting work done. With a spacious upstairs seating area, guests can enjoy quiet conversation or simply sip coffee in peace. The menu brings together savory favorites and beloved pastries, offering something delicious for every kind of craving—from soups and breads to croissants and macarons.

  • Macarons, brownies & cookies

Reviews

Sara I. (Dec 30, 2024): 

“This is such a cozy and lovely location of Common Bond Bistro & Bakery.


In fact, this location is probably my favorite within the greater Houston area! It is so open, colorful, warm and inviting with the café. Nestled within the vibrant and upbeat neighborhood of Tanglewood. They've got plenty of indoor garage parking that is steps away from the café. Perfect. No need to fight for parking. A quiet and serene location that surrounds itself within the grounds of an apartment building. This location in particular opened up over the previous summer season, and until then, it remains clean with friendly and cordial customer service. Give this location a try, you will love it. They also have a quiet section upstairs where you can chat over coffee and conversations... you get what I'm sayin?

title: Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine – A Flavor-Packed South Indian Gem in Spring Branch
description: Spring Branch may not be the first neighborhood that comes to mind for standout Indian food, but Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine is changing that narrative in the best way possible. Despite being a relatively new restaurant, this spot is already poppin’—thanks to its rich flavors, warm hospitality, and authentic South Indian cooking. Everything from the service to the atmosphere feels welcoming, and the food delivers comfort and excitement in equal measure.The menu highlights traditional favorites prepar
author: Sara Loren
html:
Spring Branch may not be the first neighborhood that comes to mind for standout Indian food, but Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine is changing that narrative in the best way possible. Despite being a relatively new restaurant, this spot is already poppin’—thanks to its rich flavors, warm hospitality, and authentic South Indian cooking. Everything from the service to the atmosphere feels welcoming, and the food delivers comfort and excitement in equal measure.


The menu highlights traditional favorites prepared with care by South Indian chefs, and the results are incredible: crisp dosas, fragrant biryanis, flavorful chutneys, and satisfying appetizers. With generous portions and bold spices, Ruchi’s offers a dining experience that feels both homey and celebratory. Add lively music videos and travel shows playing in the background, and the whole restaurant buzzes with joy.


Must-Try Items:

  • Masala Dosa with coconut chutney, sambar & kurma

  • Meat-filled, spice-rich Biryani

  • Veggie samosas with yogurt mint chutney & tamarind chutney

  • Ras Malai topped with pistachios & dried rose petals

  • Chai during a lunch visit


Reviews

Sara I. (Oct 6, 2024): 

“I don't think this restaurant has even been opened for a year but man it’s poppin’, the flavors, the service, everything. This gem of a spot is located within the Spring Branch area… a part of town that’s typically not known for Indian food. Everything about Ruchi's was perfect. Down to their service, warm environment and tantalizing food. Wow! I asked the Non-Indian servers if the chefs were Indian.. and she said yes.. in fact they are South Indian.


Perfect! No wonder the Masala Dosa hit the spot. Huge, full of savory potato filling and complemented with coconut sambar, kurma, etc.


Biryani was pretty good as well. Full of meat, spices and savory goodness. I was amazed at how much food was left over after everyone ate. The food was so delicious that everyone continued to peck at their plates. We got full quick, generous servings that were packed full of flavor. We also like the appetizers served in the beginning, potato veggie samosas that were complemented with green yogurt chutney and tamarind chutney.

Lastly, we enjoyed the Ras Malai, a sweet cottage cheese dumpling dessert that's soaked in a milky saffron base, topped with crushed pistachios and dried rose flowers. Sweet closing to sum up a warm fun-filled night.

All in all, everyone had a good time at this cute little spot tucked out in S.B. They have TVs with colorful music blasting, as well as food travel shows.


Thanks for the warm service and wonderful hospitality. We will surely revisit next time around, perhaps during lunch while sipping on chai and such!

Until next time. ~xoxoxo~”



Category: Indian 

Location: Spring Branch, Houston 


Tags: Ruchi’s Indian Cuisine Houston, South Indian food Houston, best dosa Houston, Spring Branch restaurants, Indian biryani Houston, Ras Malai Houston

title: Windmill Market & Produce – The Iconic Date Shake Stop of North Palm Springs
description: There are road trip treats—and then there are Palm Springs date shakes, the kind that feel like a rite of passage when traveling through the desert. Windmill Market & Produce, nestled among the iconic spinning turbines of North Palm Springs, serves one of the most memorable versions you’ll taste: thick, creamy, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.Made with fresh locally grown dates, their classic vanilla date shake is rich in flavor with warm caramel notes that taste almost like brown sugar melting
author: Sara Loren
html:
There are road trip treats—and then there are Palm Springs date shakes, the kind that feel like a rite of passage when traveling through the desert. Windmill Market & Produce, nestled among the iconic spinning turbines of North Palm Springs, serves one of the most memorable versions you’ll taste: thick, creamy, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.


Made with fresh locally grown dates, their classic vanilla date shake is rich in flavor with warm caramel notes that taste almost like brown sugar melting into cold cream. The texture is luscious and velvety, and the dates practically dissolve on the tongue. It’s the perfect refreshment after exploring Joshua Tree or cruising through the Yucca Valley.


Beyond shakes, the market sells beautifully packaged fresh dates—ideal for snacking or gifting. The coconut-rolled dates are a standout, offering a sweet, tropical twist. Friendly and efficient service adds to the charm, making it an easy and comforting stop during a desert drive.


Windmill Market is a slice of local flavor infused with a sense of place—surrounded by towering windmills, sunbaked mountains, and all the nostalgic vibes of a classic California road trip.


Must-Try Items:

  • Vanilla ice cream fresh date shake (the original, the icon)

  • Coconut-rolled dates

  • Other fresh date varieties to take home


Review

Sara I. (Mar 3, 2023):

 “The fresh date shake here was marvelous.. thick in viscosity, creamy and out of this world. The aroma reminded me of brown sugar and the flavor was warm, even though it was a cold and creamy milkshake. They use fresh dates that are commonly grown near and around the palm springs area.


We didn't get to venture too deep within Palm Springs, but this was the closest market to us when we were venturing out of Joshua Tree. Folks were friendly and efficient with their service. We opted for the vanilla ice cream date shake, which is the original flavor here. The dates just melt in your mouth and are totally otherworldly, along with the fresh packaged dates that you can purchase here. They make for a great gift as well, and there are plenty of different flavors — my favorite being the dates rolled in dessicated coconut.


All in all, this is a pretty neat spot. I'd love to revisit and try their savory foods and other items as well.


Geographically, it's super cool to be surrounded by windmills nearby, literally and figuratively. When around and passing through the Yucca Valley, you can count on Windmill Market & Produce for a great beverage and perhaps a snack or two while cruising through your road trip. :) Until next time!”



Category: Grocery, Fruits & Veggies, Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt 

Location: North Palm Springs, California

title: Joe & The Juice – A Refreshing Airport Pick-Me-Up in St. Paul
description: Joe & The Juice brings a touch of Scandinavian café culture to the Minneapolis–St. Paul airport, offering travelers a vibrant, modern stop for juices, coffees, sandwiches, and refreshing pick-me-ups on the go. For those familiar with the brand’s global presence—especially in Norway and across Europe—this location rekindles a little international nostalgia amid the airport bustle.While the shop is known for both its “Joe” (coffee) and its “Juice,” the iced matcha latte hits a perfect balance: cre
author: Sara Loren
html:
Joe & The Juice brings a touch of Scandinavian café culture to the Minneapolis–St. Paul airport, offering travelers a vibrant, modern stop for juices, coffees, sandwiches, and refreshing pick-me-ups on the go. For those familiar with the brand’s global presence—especially in Norway and across Europe—this location rekindles a little international nostalgia amid the airport bustle.


While the shop is known for both its “Joe” (coffee) and its “Juice,” the iced matcha latte hits a perfect balance: creamy, lightly sweetened, and vividly green. It’s a wonderful alternative to the standard airport chains, providing a cool, refreshing moment before boarding. Service, though friendly, was a bit rushed, resulting in a small hiccup with the drink size—but the team corrected it quickly and without hesitation.


What to Try:

  • Iced Matcha Latte (bright, creamy & refreshing)

  • Sandwiches & juices for a quick airport meal

  • Specialty beverages for something different than the usual airport fare


Joe & The Juice remains a reliable go-to for travelers craving fresh flavors and modern café vibes. With a bit more attention to detail during busy rushes, this location could shine even brighter.


Review

Sara I. (May 17, 2023):

“I was thrilled to spot Joe & The Juice recently within my Minneapolis airport excursion whilst running to my gate in time. Hadn't been to a Joe and the Juice cafe in a few years. Throughout my travels in Europe (particularly within Scandinavia) I would frequent this cafe. They had em all over Norway. I do recall visiting a location or two within New York as well a few years back. Needless to say, it had been a while since I had a Joe fix.


The menu still looked the same as it does throughout the world and their sandwiches looked decent as well. I did not opt for coffee or food, rather I opted for their iced matcha latte. I know.. this spot is known for their ‘joe’ but they're just as popular for their ‘juice’ hence the name!! Felt the need to cool down so an iced matcha latte did the trick. It was creamy, lightly sweetened and refreshing. Just the right hue of bright green within the cup and I sipped away while on my excursion.


The service was just OK though and they seemed super busy. Yeah I know it's the airport but they really weren't fixating on the details. I initially ordered a medium beverage, but they gave me a small one instead. This caught my eye immediately and I told them to remake my drink. They did without any hesitation. I was glad to have my medium sized iced drink as I was sharing it with my favorite person. Mm crisp matcha moments! Something different than Starbucks, thank goodness.


This might be their only location in MN? Not sure. It was busy. I'll revisit in the near future. Just glad this airport has a few options besides SB — what a refreshing change. To the workers that work at this location, please focus on details and keep this place clean and non-disheveled. Bbyes.”


Category: Sandwiches, Coffee & Tea, Juice Bars & Smoothies 

Location: St. Paul, MN 


Tags: Joe & The Juice review, St. Paul airport coffee, matcha latte MSP, Scandinavian café chains, airport drink options, Joe & The Juice sandwiches

author: Sara Loren
html:
SomiSomi in Katy delivers the kind of soft-serve experience that’s equal parts nostalgic, playful, and indulgently creamy. Though the interior is small—much like most of their locations—the grab-and-go setup works perfectly for this bustling dessert spot. Lines may form quickly, but they move fast, and the reward of warm taiyaki paired with cold, silky soft serve is always worth it.


This location shines with its rotating flavors, offering something new and exciting on every visit. From classic staples to unique seasonal blends, SomiSomi keeps dessert lovers curious and coming back. The Korean-style soft serve is velvety, milky, lightly sweet, and wonderfully airy—ideal for customizing with toppings, fillings, and that iconic fish-shaped waffle cone.


Must-Try Items:

  • Korean-style soft serve (milky, fluffy & not overly sweet)

  • Seasonal flavors — sweet corn + horchata

  • Taiyaki waffle filled with vanilla custard

  • Matcha-dusted soft serve

  • Any swirl or mix for added creaminess


Review

Sara I. (Nov 2, 2024): 

“SomiSomi is so so yummy yummy.


I'm liking this location out in Katy. A little small within the interior, but most locations seem to be that way. It's a grab and go ice cream spot that fills up quickly. The lines are long yet it moves rather fast. Customer service is good and you get to watch your dessert being made. I've always liked Korean style soft serve. So fluffy, soft and creamy. Very milky as well and not too sweet. They seem to often have a new flavor and that is what I like about this spot. They had a sweet corn flavor mixed with their horchata flavor and it was good. A bit more on the mellow side but it still has a nice aroma and flavor. Their crispy fish shaped waffle is so yummy. I love loading it up with vanilla custard. Their dusting of matcha on top of soft serve is chef's kiss. Flavors are good and portions are plenty.


You can't go wrong with SomiSomi as a cooling and creamy dessert option after having savory bite to eat within the area. With so much to see and do in this part of town, it's no wonder that SomiSomi is on the list for something delectable while out in this part of town. Creamy and dreamy. Until we meet again!”

title: Carter’s – A Bright, Standalone Gem for Baby & Toddler Clothing in Sugar Land
description: This standalone Carter’s in Sugar Land is a breath of fresh air for parents who prefer to shop in person rather than rely solely on online browsing. Unlike the usual mall or Galleria locations, this spacious storefront offers convenience, warmth, and a refreshingly hands-on shopping experience. With friendly customer service and a vivid selection of clothing, it’s an ideal stop for parents stocking up on essentials or refreshing seasonal wardrobes.Being able to feel fabrics, compare sizes, and h
author: Sara Loren
html:
This standalone Carter’s in Sugar Land is a breath of fresh air for parents who prefer to shop in person rather than rely solely on online browsing. Unlike the usual mall or Galleria locations, this spacious storefront offers convenience, warmth, and a refreshingly hands-on shopping experience. With friendly customer service and a vivid selection of clothing, it’s an ideal stop for parents stocking up on essentials or refreshing seasonal wardrobes.


Being able to feel fabrics, compare sizes, and hold outfits up to your little one makes a world of difference—especially since kids grow quickly and the fit of Carter’s clothing can vary after washing. Luckily, the staff is attentive and happy to answer questions, ensuring families confidently pick the right items and sizes. Fall and winter apparel, cozy layers, and adorable accessories fill the displays, making this store especially fun to browse during cooler months.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Standalone location with wide, easy-to-browse layout

  • Helpful staff offering sizing & care tips

  • Abundant seasonal collections, from beanies to bibs

  • Great prices and tons of patterns & colors

  • Perfect for parents who prefer in-person shopping

  • Large selection that easily fills an hour of browsing


Reviews

Sara I. (Sep 26, 2024 – First to Review): 

“This is such a wonderful location of Carter's; from the warm customer service to the vivid selection of clothing they've got for tots and babes.


I don't typically find brick and mortar locations of Carter's unless they are tucked away inside some mall or Galleria type location.


The physical presence of this stand alone Carter's makes it worth visiting. They have a good online selection, but in all honesty, it is better to visually see and try the clothing in person for your little one. Sometimes what you see online is what you don't get.


Children typically grow out of clothing rather quickly. Carter’s clothing can shrink in size and is not of the splendor variety that will hold its shape and structure forever. Therefore, size up and wash those clothing in cold water! Oh and not everything can be thrown into the dryer, depending on the type of fabric or style of clothing. As mentioned earlier, the customer service here is great and you can ask them anything in regards to their products.


I am already loving their autumn and winter apparel. Prices are excellent, patterns are plenty, and they have so many styles and colors for the little one. Loving their beanies, socks, bibs and other niknaks in between.

This is a great retail shop, their hours are good and their selection is massive. One could easily take an hour just browsing their variety and trying it on their little bean. I have already picked up beanies and jumpers for autumn.


Google might say that this Carter's location is closed, but it is definitely open. If you are in the area, go check it out and see for yourself!”

Milk+Sugar is beloved for its dreamy, thoughtfully crafted flavors—playfully named and even more delightful to taste. While certain limited-time flavors can rotate out quickly (pandan lovers, we feel you!), the classics remain as creamy, smooth, and nostalgic as ever. The event included a waffle cone, making that first crisp crunch especially satisfying on a humid night.


Event Highlights:

  • Spacious, bright new location

  • Smooth, delicious flavors with whimsical names (Heart of Glass forever!)

  • Generous sampling & friendly staff

  • Complimentary waffle cone treat

  • Perfect cool-down dessert on a warm Houston evening


Review

Sara I. (Jun 12, 2024):

“Mmm mmm milk + sugar! I think most of us are familiar with this adorable ice cream shoppe? I know that I am. But this new location in specific is a lot larger, brighter and cleaner than their original location. I still like their OG shoppe.. but this one? Absolutely ideal with location (geographically) as well as their huge parking lot that they share with several other store fronts.


I have always loved the flavors @ milk + sugar. They are dreamy as well as the namesake of each flavor. Heart of Glass? So cute. Still a favorite flavor for moi and @ this location, it tasted just the same. The kids slingin' the ice cream allowed us to sample a few. I was already familiar with most of their flavors so just opted for my favs. Sweet n' delectable, smooth ice cream. I was really hoping to try their pandan flavor for the month of HAPI, but alas, it wasn't available on a Saturday night. I've had pandan ice cream elsewhere, so I'm hoping to catch this one here next time around.


It was a generous sweet treat that included a waffle cone. Cold dessert on a humid night. Crunch. Munch. Yum.

It was perf' in every way. Until next time!”

title: The Ismaili Center, Houston — A Calm, Beautiful Cultural Stop in the City
description: Some places make you slow down the second you arrive and The Ismaili Center in Houston is exactly that kind of space. Set in Fourth Ward, it feels peaceful and intentional, with the kind of atmosphere that invites you to wander, notice the details, and simply enjoy being there. Even if you’ve never visited before, the experience is laid out in a way that feels welcoming and easy to follow.Arrival is smooth and well managed. At the time of this visit, entry was routed through the W Dallas St gate
author: Mark Wang
html:
Some places make you slow down the second you arrive and The Ismaili Center in Houston is exactly that kind of space. Set in Fourth Ward, it feels peaceful and intentional, with the kind of atmosphere that invites you to wander, notice the details, and simply enjoy being there. Even if you’ve never visited before, the experience is laid out in a way that feels welcoming and easy to follow.


Arrival is smooth and well managed. At the time of this visit, entry was routed through the W Dallas St gate, where a guard helped direct cars and guided visitors to parking. From there, you’ll park in the garage below, then take the elevator up to the first floor to check in. Simple, clear, and orderly.


If you’re visiting on a weekend, the free tour is one of the best parts. You’ll be assigned a tour group (with a color lanyard) and guided through an informative overview that helps you understand the layout before exploring on your own. It sets a calm tone for the rest of the visit because you’re not spending time guessing where to go next.


Plan for walking: the grounds are expansive, and you’ll likely cover more distance than expected. If needed, wheelchair service is available, which can make the visit far more comfortable. Security was noticeable during this visit as well, adding structure and reassurance without taking away from the peaceful vibe.


One quick heads-up: the café was not open yet at the time of this visit, so if you’re planning a longer stop, consider grabbing a drink or snack beforehand.


What to Know + What to Do


  • Open-to-everyone cultural and community space: calm, welcoming, and visitor-friendly

  • Enter via W Dallas St (open gate at time of review) and follow staff guidance for a smooth arrival

  • Park in the downstairs garage, then take the elevator to the first floor to check in

  • Take the free weekend tour first (you’ll get a color lanyard for your group) to learn the layout

  • Wear comfortable shoes, there’s a lot of ground to cover

  • Ask about wheelchair service if you need support navigating the distance

  • Plan food separately (the café was not open at the time of this visit)

  • Expect visible security, organized and reassuring, not disruptive


Review

Mark Wang — Tradition Local Contributor

Date: Dec 20, 2025


“It is a very beautiful culture and community center, that is open to everyone to use and enjoy. Right now, they have only one entrance gate open, which is on W Dallas St. There is a guard that will guide you where to park your car, it is very easy to navigate here. After you park downstairs in the garage you can take the elevator to the first flood to check-in. On the weekend, they are having a free tour for the visitors. They also have wheelchair service if you need a wheelchair because there is a lot of ground to cover here. For the tour, they will give you a tour group assigned color lanyard. The tour was very informative and you get to get a good sense of the layout so you can explore the rest of the place by yourself. There is a good amount of security at this time.


At this time the cafe is not open yet.”



Quick Answers (AEO)


Is The Ismaili Center in Houston open to the public?

Yes. According to this visit, it’s open to everyone to use and enjoy.


Where do you enter?

At the time of this visit, the open entrance gate was on W Dallas St.


Is there parking?

Yes. Parking is in the downstairs garage, and a guard helps guide you.


How do you check in?

Take the elevator to the first floor to check in.


Are there tours?

Yes. Free tours are available on weekends.


Is it wheelchair accessible?

Wheelchair service is available, which helps because the grounds are large.


Is the café open?

Not at the time of this visit.


Visit their Website: https://ismailicenter.org/

html:
The R&B Tea Community Meetup in Sugar Land was a bright and flavorful start to the week, offering delicious boba beverages and warm hospitality. Known for their high-quality drinks and consistently friendly service, this R&B Tea location proved to be the perfect spot for a relaxed afternoon treat—especially on a warm Texas Monday.


With a menu full of customizable drinks, guests had plenty of options to explore. The standout order of the day was a strawberry matcha fresh milk tea with tapioca, balanced at 70% sweetness for the ideal blend of earthy matcha and bright fruitiness. As always, R&B’s tapioca pearls delivered that signature chewy bite and rich flavor, making every sip satisfying.


Event Highlights:

  • Friendly, attentive staff (shoutout to Brandon & Julia)

  • Strawberry matcha fresh milk tea with perfectly chewy tapioca

  • Great customization options for sweetness & mix-ins

  • Consistent beverage quality and flavorful milk teas

  • A fun community gathering on a warm afternoon

  • Ideal Monday pick-me-up with caffeine + comfort


Review

Sara I. (May 20, 2024):

“It was great to visit this spot for community week! I didn't even know community week was a thing and thought this was an ‘elite week’ sorta deal. Nope! More boba tea for all!


R&B has some tasty beverage choices and it was not my first time visiting this spot within the land of Sugar. Quality of beverages and customer service is spot on. Brandon and Julia were friendly and answered any of the questions I had in mind. I ordered a fresh milk beverage (strawberry matcha tea with tapioca). Asked for half sweet, but Brandon mentioned the matcha is quite strong and bitter. Bumped it to 70% sweetness and it was perfect! R&B tapioca is always chewy with the right texture and flavor. All in all, the matcha blended well with the bright flavors of strawberry. Will definitely reorder this next time! Their milk teas in general are great. Plenty of options for flavors, mixins and toppings.


This was a great spot to visit on a warm Monday afternoon. Getting the week started with a tasty caffeinated fix!


 Until next time! SYOY. :)”

Located within the Montrose Collective, this airy, modern scoop shop is known for its ultra-creamy textures, inventive flavors, and clean, welcoming interior. Guests can sample flavors using metal tasting spoons (a fun, eco-friendly twist), then settle in for a treat inside the cozy seating area. Whether you're mixing flavors, indulging in a sundae, or sipping on a nostalgic soda, Van Leeuwen serves up simple joys in every scoop.

  • Coffee Affogato Ice Cream

  • Dark Chocolate Brownie Ice Cream

  • Texas Rodeo Sundae

  • Root Beer Soda


Review

Sara I. (Jun 18, 2022):

“Loved this little sweet elite perk! This ice cream spot is bright and cheery, perfect on this sunny Saturday visit. I've been to V.L. before, and the establishment was just as nice and clean, well organized like last time. The lines were non existent, so Lou and I grabbed our ice cream and got to comfortably sit indoors.


The scooper was friendly and allowed us to try a few samples. I went for the coffee affogato flavor and the dark chocolate brownie flavor. Out of the two, the affogato was creamier and lush with a nice light coffee flavor. The brownie ice cream was a bit on the drier side but still tasty.


We also tried the Texas rodeo sundae and root beer soda. Flavors were great—dreamy, creamy, crunchy, and nostalgic. Overall we had a great time. Until next time!”

title: The Oceanaire Seafood Room – A Classic Galleria Spot with a Mixed HRW Experience
description: The Oceanaire Seafood Room is a long-standing Galleria favorite—known for its sleek, submarine-inspired design, large corner windows overlooking bustling streets, and over two decades of reputation as a premier seafood destination. It’s the kind of restaurant many Houstonians keep on their “must-visit” list. During Houston Restaurant Weeks, expectations run especially high, but this particular visit offered a mix of highs and lows.While the ambiance and several dishes impressed, service inconsis
author: Sara Loren
html:
The Oceanaire Seafood Room is a long-standing Galleria favorite—known for its sleek, submarine-inspired design, large corner windows overlooking bustling streets, and over two decades of reputation as a premier seafood destination. It’s the kind of restaurant many Houstonians keep on their “must-visit” list. During Houston Restaurant Weeks, expectations run especially high, but this particular visit offered a mix of highs and lows.

While the ambiance and several dishes impressed, service inconsistencies impacted the overall experience. Still, the restaurant’s strengths—fresh sushi, flavorful appetizers, and a stellar key lime pie—hint at its potential when firing on all cylinders. With such an iconic Houston presence, a return visit to explore the regular menu feels worthwhile.


Highlights & Notes:

  • Iconic Galleria location with a submarine-inspired aesthetic

  • Fresh, flavorful sushi & excellent smoked salmon starter

  • Tasty shrimp fried rice, though served lukewarm due to service delays

  • Key lime pie: tart, refreshing, and one of the best

  • Service during HRW was inattentive and lacked communication

  • Regular menu appears strong—worth revisiting outside HRW


Reviews

Sara I. (Sep 12, 2023): 

“3 stars experience during Houston Restaurant Weeks. Boy, were we all excited to dine in at this restaurant. It is a Houston classic!


From the submarine looking terrain, to the large windows at the corner facing one of the busiest streets in Houston. It's the Galleria after all, and it’s one of the most popular spots to visit. This restaurant has been around for over 20 years, and for some of us, it was our very first time.


I do believe they could have had better choices in regards to their food menu with HRW. This is all in regards to food allergies, mind you. So that’s something we take seriously. But we came on a mission! To dine in on HRW style menu which benefits the local Houston Food Bank.


Their regular menu looks great and appealing. We may revisit and try items from their everyday menu. We did try their sushi and we loved it. The sushi was fresh and flavorful. It retained its shape well and came with a burst of flavor. My second favorite was the smoked salmon. It was chunky, held its shape and it had a great umami yet mellow flavor as well. Paired well with the bold marinated onions, capers, relish and crispy crackers.

I did like the shrimp fried rice, it was flavorful and well seasoned — however it was quite lukewarm by the time it reached our table. Reason being? They forgot to deliver our order to the table. We waited for ages after being served appetizers. So much time passed by that I had to flag down a waiter from far away, just to get his notice and ask him what happened to our food?


He quickly went in, back of the house and grabbed our meals. So basically our meals were sitting BOH, chillin and getting cold. No apologies or ‘I'm sorry for the delay in your food.’ Instead he mentioned, ‘Oh, we're packed and having a busy day here.’ Definitely didn't seem like it, with most of the room being empty. Just one day before, my entire office dined in here for HRW. What must have happened then? Not enough employees to accommodate diners needs. Lack of customer service was the downfall of our experience dining here at the Oceanaire.


Dessert was good. It was ordered from their regular menu as it’s not provided with HRW. We opted for the key lime pie and it was definitely one of the better ones we've all had. Super tart, sweet and refreshing. Perfect on the palate after consuming mellow oceanic foods.


Again, we all enjoyed our food. Totally look forward to revisiting and trying items from their regular menu. This is a nice spot to bring out-of-town guests. They have many non-seafood items as well for those that aren't much into seafood. We're just hoping for warmer and keen attentive service next time around for such a posh and elaborate spot such as this. Until next time!”



Category: Seafood 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston 


Tags: Oceanaire Houston review, Houston Restaurant Weeks dining, Galleria seafood restaurants, upscale dining Houston, smoked salmon Houston, key lime pie Houston

title: Sunday Press – A Colorful, Flavor-Packed Café in Garden Oaks
description: Sunday Press is a vibrant, joyful café that feels like a burst of color from the moment you walk in. With an extensive menu, beautiful pastry displays, and a warm neighborhood buzz, this Garden Oaks staple delivers a little something for everyone—whether you're craving a latte, a comfort-filled breakfast taco, or a sweet afternoon treat. author: Sara Loren
html:
Sunday Press is a vibrant, joyful café that feels like a burst of color from the moment you walk in. With an extensive menu, beautiful pastry displays, and a warm neighborhood buzz, this Garden Oaks staple delivers a little something for everyone—whether you're craving a latte, a comfort-filled breakfast taco, or a sweet afternoon treat. Sunday Press fills up quickly, especially in the mornings, but the variety of seating and the energy inside make it a welcoming spot for conversations, studying, remote work, or slow weekend lounging.


The pastry case alone is enough to spark childhood nostalgia and adult-level excitement: marble pound cake, macadamia nut cookies, snickerdoodles, and the rare, highly coveted swirl croissants. The matcha swirl croissant in particular stands out—crispy, flaky, and filled with a balanced earthy sweetness. Drinks are equally satisfying, with the London fog latte offering depth, sweetness, and the subtle kiss of bergamot on creamy foam.


Must-Try Items:

  • Matcha swirl croissant

  • London fog latte

  • Breakfast taco (warm, hearty & veggie-loaded)

  • Cookies, pound cakes & pastries behind the glass

  • Acai bowls, soups, salads, and sandwiches


Review

Sara I. (Sep 6, 2023 – ROTD Dec 30, 2023): 

“My gosh — the menu here is so colorful, fun and quite extensive. You will find something for everyone here! Rejoice. This colorful café in more ways than one is serving up colorful, sweet and intricate food items.


Upon first glance — it's their sweets and treats that keep me coming back for more. Been awhile since I glanced at a marble pound cake, macadamia nut cookie, snickerdoodle and swirly croissants all tucked behind a lovely glass display. Sunday Press has these one of a kind swirl croissants which are hard to find within the city of Houston. This spot serves up these rare gems and on top of that? They're quite good. Great YUM and CRISP factor with the right amount of filling of your choice — my fav being the matcha swirl croissant.


For drinks selections: they've got everything you need! From café lattes, tea lattes and many other beverages to choose from — ours being the london fog latte. Sweet. Depth. And just the right amount of bergamot essence kissing the milky foam of the cup.


In regards to food, you'll find sandwiches, soups, salad among many other items. It's almost hard to decide — I was torn between pasta salad or breakfast taco. I went for the brekkie taco and glad I did. It was one taco yet it was filling, warm and with plenty of flavor. I liked how the taco wasn't spicy and that the tortilla was warm, stretchy and fresh. They added plenty of shredded veggies to my veggie breakfast taco. It was filling and made for the perfect meal earlier in the day. If I'm ever here later in the day, I'll definitely opt for some type of salad to go with my tea.


This spot fills up quick! We got here earlier in the morning and witnessed seats disappearing fast. Thankfully they have plenty of seating of all types. Many folks connecting and chatting while others studying or working on their laptops. With decently warm service within a unique colorful environment — I can definitely see why this place slowly causes traffic jams and gets packed within the day.


I envision myself revisiting again sometime soon and ordering a few different items on the menu. Will be back when in the area, which is once in awhile. Thank you Sunday Press for your treats and good vibes.”



Category: Coffee & Tea, Acai Bowls, Sandwiches 

Location: Oak Forest / Garden Oaks, Houston 


Tags: Sunday Press Houston, Garden Oaks cafés, swirl croissants Houston, best London fog latte Houston, colorful cafés Texas, breakfast tacos Houston

description: Coffee Mill is one of those charming, blink-and-you’ll-miss-it cafés tucked quietly into the bustle of the Galleria area. author: Sara Loren
html:
Coffee Mill is one of those charming, blink-and-you’ll-miss-it cafés tucked quietly into the bustle of the Galleria area. What appears from the outside to be just a coffee bean retailer is actually a cozy sit-down spot—with an unexpected twist: it’s directly connected to Kolache Factory. That means fresh local coffee and warm kolaches in one convenient stop.


Guests can order their drink at the counter, turn around, and pick up kolaches from the adjoining side—a delightful setup for breakfast lovers and snack seekers alike. The kolaches are consistently warm, generously filled, and flavorful, available in both savory and sweet varieties. Pair them with Coffee Mill’s smooth Katz Coffee beverages—locally roasted and wonderfully aromatic—and you’ve got a simple yet satisfying experience


Must-Try Items:

  • Iced caffe latte (half sweet with vanilla — creamy & balanced)

  • Chicken enchilada kolache

  • Spinach kolache

  • Sweet fruit kolaches, cream cheese kolaches & cinnamon rolls

  • Freshly brewed Katz Coffee drinks


Whether you’re stopping by early for the best pastry selection or grabbing a quick iced latte to beat the Houston heat, Coffee Mill brings local flavor and low-key charm to the Galleria neighborhood.


Review

Sara I. (Aug 8, 2023):

 “I like this spot! It's a bit of a hole in the wall. It's super quick to pass by and you can easily miss it. All these years I thought this place only sold coffee beans but it's actually a sit down cafe. What's unique about Coffee Mill is that it's connected with Kolache Factory. You can order coffee right up at the corner, then turn around, and order kolaches from the other side of the cafe.


Kolaches are many in flavor and are filling in size and always warm. Service is good and they always warm up the kolaches for customers. My favorite is the chicken enchilada kolache as well as the spinach kolache. Both look small in size but they're actually packed with filling and flavor. I've never had any products from any other kolache factory, so I can't compare... But I like the selection this location has.


These days I adore their iced caffe latte. It's creamy, fragrant and light. It's not like those iced coffees that are super strong and bitter in flavor. I ask them to make it half sweet with vanilla and it's perfect in flavor. They use Katz coffee here and the beans are local which is something I always support. Go for the local!


So glad to have this spot close by within the Galleria area to grab a snack and some type of coffee. If you visit earlier in the day, you'll get a better selection of their baked goods. They also serve up cream cheese kolaches, sweet fruit kolaches and cinnamon rolls. Will revisit when needing an iced caffe latte and a bite to eat in this heat. Until next time!”



Category: Coffee & Tea 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston 


Tags: Coffee Mill Houston, Galleria coffee shops, kolaches Houston, Katz Coffee Houston, hidden cafés Houston, breakfast kolaches Galleria

author: Sara Loren
html:
The FACE FOUNDRIÉ self-care event in West University offered a calming, restorative, and deeply pampering experience—an ideal way to close out a long week. Bright, airy, and filled with natural light, the studio created an inviting environment that immediately set the tone for relaxation. The soft aroma in the air, paired with warm hospitality, made every guest feel welcomed and unrushed.


Snacks and tea were available prior to treatments, allowing guests to settle in slowly and savor the moment. Once the facial began, the experience blossomed into something extraordinary—thoughtfully curated, sensory-rich, and delivered with care. From aromatherapy to facial cupping to the decadent cocoa butter option, every detail elevated the treatment. The addition of scalp massages and a cozy weighted blanket made the service feel even more nurturing.


Event Highlights:

  • Bright, natural-light–filled spa environment

  • Complimentary tea & snacks before treatments

  • Exceptional service from knowledgeable facialists

  • Aromatherapy, facial cupping & cocoa butter enhancement

  • Clean, calming facilities

  • Weighted blanket + head massage for total relaxation

  • Gift cards & membership options for ongoing pampering


Review

Sara I. (Oct 3, 2023):

“My goodness, I loved everything about this experience... it was different and unique. A cosy sort of experience that was wrapped around nurturing and pampering. I have always loved perks that were centered around food. But this one? Yeah, it hit differently. & it was exactly what was needed on a Friday, a perfect way to end the week by getting a facial close to evening time.


Right from the start, upon walking in, I knew that I would love this spot. It was bright, airy and quite roomy. I love how this spot uses as much natural light as possible, instead of keeping it dim. The aroma was fresh and inviting and the service was just as warm. They have snacks and tea to choose from before getting your facial. My facialist was busy arranging everything in the beginning so I made myself a nice snack and tea to munch on. I was not running hastily on time and wanted the pleasure of soaking in this experience.


Once the facial got started, I knew that I was in for a real treat. Every single thing about this facial treatment was mind-blowingly amazing. I had received a facial one month prior to this experience at another spot. It was good. But this one? It took the cake. From the beginning of service, til the end, my facialist, Drea, was knowledgeable and geared for great service. The aromatherapy used was one to delight the senses and tickle the soul. I loved the facial cupping that was used as well. & the aromatic cocoa butter which I opted for.


I was often asked if everything was okay and if I was comfortable. It was nice for Drea to check in on me from time to time. Facilities here are clean, including their restrooms. I loved how my facialist took her time to give me the best pampering service. Nothing was rushed here.


Throughout the session I would get a scalp/head massage and was also given a weighted blanket that made me feel oh so cosy and snug. I was wrapped up like a burrito with nowhere to move. Perfect.


Will I be back here? Most definitely. Service was great from all those that were working here that day. As mentioned, my experience here was perfect and one that I am grateful for. They also have gift cards here if you want to get one for family or friends. You can also sign up and become a member for recurrent facials.


This was one for the books. So nourishing, deep down in all aspects. SYOY!”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Category: Bakeries 

Location: Spring Branch, Houston 


Magnol French Baking is one of Houston’s most delightful hidden gems—a true Parisian-inspired treasure tucked inside an industrial pocket of Spring Branch. Unassuming from the outside, this bakery transforms the moment you step through the door: the aroma of butter, warm pastries, and fragrant coffee instantly transports you to a cozy corner of France. Small, bustling, and beloved by those “in the know,” Magnol offers some of the city’s most authentically French baked goods.


Arriving early is essential, as pastries sell out with surprising speed. By 8:45 a.m., trays were already emptying—always a sign of a bakery doing something very, very right. Inside, the atmosphere is bright, airy, and inviting, a striking contrast to its discreet exterior. Imported French jams, honeys, and small treats line the shelves, adding to its boutique charm. Whether you’re craving a flaky pastry, a warm drink, or a moment of morning bliss, Magnol delivers.


Must-Try Items:

  • Pain aux raisins (flaky, crisp & beautifully creamy inside)

  • Madeleines (soft, buttery shell-shaped cakes)

  • Croissants — assorted varieties

  • Linzer cookies

  • Tea lattes & fragrant coffee


Review

Sara I. (Feb 12, 2024 – ROTD Apr 19, 2024): 

“Incredibly tasty, very buttery and authentically French. Magnol Bakery is a true hole in the wall spot.


This spot is located within a discrete and rather industrial part of town. You'll be sure to miss it if speeding past the area. I did not even know this bakery existed until a good friend brought up within a conversation. TY for sharing a piece of mini France in Houston, otherwise I would have never known about this place! It's best to arrive early, as baked goods run out quick. To my surprise, many items were disappearing from shelves around 8:45 a.m. Should I have visited even earlier in the morning? Most likely. This place is packed and quite popular... basically if you're within the know, so you'll know.


The pain aux raisins (flaky puffed pastry rolled with raisins and vanilla crème) was an absolute delight... great crisp and texture. The madeleines (shell shaped butter cakes) were quite nice as well. Their cozy and warm tea lattes as well as coffee was quite fragrant and paired well with the baked treats.


This spot isn't too big from the inside so the line was literally wrapped within the interior of the café. The interior is light and airy, as opposed to the outside of the building. Tucked within one small shelf... they have a few food products for purchase that are imported from France (ie; fruit jam, honey, etc.)


I would love to revisit again... (even earlier in the morning) and try their various croissants, linzer cookie and cute little cakes. They have a few other caffeinated drink options as well to warm up your day. No better moments than visiting during winter or spring season! Thanks Magnol for brightening up my morning.. I'll be sure to visit again. Until we meet again — Au Revoir!”


Tags: Magnol French Baking Houston, French bakeries Houston, authentic croissants Houston, pain aux raisins Houston, Spring Branch pastries, hidden gem bakeries Houston

With only a handful of PJ’s locations in Texas, this shop serves as a rare spot to enjoy their signature roasts and seasonal treats.The menu features iced lattes, mochas, and rotating specialty drinks, with the seasonal king cake latte standing out as a festive favorite. Their made-to-order beignets arrive warm and dusted, offer
author: Sara Loren
html:
PJ’s Coffee in Pearland brings a taste of New Orleans–style brewing to the Houston suburbs, offering distinctive iced drinks, fresh beignets, and a warm café atmosphere. With only a handful of PJ’s locations in Texas, this shop serves as a rare spot to enjoy their signature roasts and seasonal treats.


The menu features iced lattes, mochas, and rotating specialty drinks, with the seasonal king cake latte standing out as a festive favorite. Their made-to-order beignets arrive warm and dusted, offering a soft, simple sweetness—pleasant, though not unforgettable. A pastry case near the register keeps cookies, muffins, and scones at the ready for a quick grab-and-go treat.


The café itself is cozy with modest seating, including sofas and smaller tables. The drive-thru is a major perk, especially for commuters or anyone in a rush. Coffee remains aromatic and satisfying, making PJ’s a solid choice for flavorful drinks outside the mainstream coffee chain circuit.


However, the biggest drawback is the ventilation. A lingering old-oil aroma and the presence of house flies can break the cozy spell and affect the overall experience. Still, with better airflow and upkeep, this location could easily elevate its charm.


Worth Trying:

  • Iced lattes & mocha drinks

  • Seasonal king cake beverages

  • Fresh, made-to-order beignets

  • Drive-thru coffee options


Atmosphere Notes:

  • Cozy interior with sofas

  • Ventilation issues & occasional flies

  • Warm service and aromatic brews


Review

Sara I. (Sep 25, 2022): 

“I like this little spot! I really do. My biggest gripe is the air ventilation and all the house flies swarming around the cafe. It literally smells like old oil in here and the ventilation is not the best. But let's get to the good stuff.. shall we?


PJs offers some unique coffee drinks and treats. There are far too few locations within the greater Houston area so it's nice to visit this particular location from time to time. I've visited another location in the past which was in another state.


They've got some great iced drinks here such as their lattes, mocha and seasonal drinks. The seasonal king cake is good here as well as their beignets. The beignets are fresh & made to order. They are decent.. nothing home to write about. The case near the register is stocked up on cookies, muffins and scones etc.


Seating is decent as well. They've got a few chairs and sofas to lounge upon.. not the biggest spot though. The drive thru will get ya in and out in a jiffy.. good for when you're in a rush. This spot is far from me so I doubt I'll be visiting anytime soon.. hoping they can open up more locations. Other than that it's a warm spot with some aromatic coffee.”



Category: Coffee & Tea 

Location: Pearland, Texas

title: Tim Hortons – A Cozy Canadian Coffee Retreat in Katy
description: Tim Hortons may be a Canadian legend, but its charming Katy outpost feels right at home in the Texas suburbs. Tucked into a quiet corner of town, this cozy café offers a nostalgic, no-fuss approach to coffee and baked treats—a welcome change from trend-heavy cafés.Famous across Canada for its reliable drip coffee, donuts, Timbits, and breakfast staples, Tim Hortons brings a touch of northern comfort to Katy. The hot coffee here is simple and satisfying, especially when paired with a tender cake
author: Sara Loren
html:
Tim Hortons may be a Canadian legend, but its charming Katy outpost feels right at home in the Texas suburbs. Tucked into a quiet corner of town, this cozy café offers a nostalgic, no-fuss approach to coffee and baked treats—a welcome change from trend-heavy cafés.


Famous across Canada for its reliable drip coffee, donuts, Timbits, and breakfast staples, Tim Hortons brings a touch of northern comfort to Katy. The hot coffee here is simple and satisfying, especially when paired with a tender cake donut dusted lightly with nutmeg—perfect for dunking. While some of the other donuts leaned a bit dry, the holiday flavors and assortment of baked goods still add to the fun.


The menu also features savory options, including avocado toast, which was just okay but offered balance among all the sweets. With festive seasonal beverages and classic cold brews available, there’s something for every type of coffee drinker.


The café’s interior is small but warm and inviting, infused with Canadian-themed décor that adds to its charm. Service is decent, though the drive-thru can get chaotic—making the dine-in experience the better choice.

Tim Hortons in Katy is a sweet little gem for a cozy winter morning, a donut-and-coffee break, or a quick suburban caffeine fix. And with more locations on the horizon, Texans may soon enjoy even more of Canada’s favorite grab-and-go coffee spot.


Must-Try Items:

  • Hot drip coffee

  • Cake donut (nutmeg-kissed, tender, perfect for dunking)

  • Seasonal/holiday drinks

  • Cold brew vanilla (if you’re in the mood for something chilled)


Review

Sara I. (Dec 5, 2022):

“Such a great little gem of a coffee shoppe tucked in a quiet corner within the suburbs of Katy, TX.

Tim Horton's is originally from Canada.. & is all the rage up in the northern hemisphere... & I can totally see why! It is considered Canada's favorite coffee on the run. This spot specializes in both hot and cold coffee drinks, as well as donuts, pastries and a few savory items.


Had heard about Tim Hortons back in the day.. just hadn't ventured out to Canada in awhile. I am glad we have a location here in TX, which is soon to spread out within neighboring cities.


Hot coffee was great.. nice and simple. Drip coffee paired with a donut? Keeping it old school. I didn't care for any cold bevvie that day.. but my friend's cold brew vanilla drink looked good. Plenty of holiday flavors this time of the year as well.


They have a variety of donuts to choose from.. my favorite being the cake donut. Tender and sprinkled a bit with nutmeg. Dunk it into hot coffee.. bliss. The other donuts were on the drier side & didn't taste fresh. That's too bad because this spot specializes in their sweet treats. Also tried their avocado toast which was just okay. I'm glad they have a bit of savory items to balance with all the sweetness.


Interior is quite small.. but cozy. Decor is quite heartwarming and very Canadian. Service was okay.. could be better. Their drive thru seemed chaotic and I totally recommend visiting the interior of the cafe.


All in all, a great spot to set up shoppe. I'll definitely revisit in the near future. Here's hoping we can get more Hortons on the way.. because ‘Horton hears a who! & A why not?!’ Lol. Totally a Dr Seuss reference.. if you know, you know. Cheers and happy coffee drinking during the coziest month of the year!”



Category: Coffee & Tea, Breakfast & Brunch, Sandwiches

Location: Katy, Texas 


Tags: Tim Hortons Katy review, Canadian coffee Texas, best donuts Katy TX, coffee shops in Katy, Tim Hortons pastries, suburban cafés Houston area

title: Jusgo Supermarket – A Bright, Wandering Marketplace in Sugar Land
description: Jusgo Supermarket is a spacious, bright, and somewhat mysterious international market—equal parts grocery store and small-business gallery. Tucked into the same plaza as 99 Ranch Market, it offers a quieter, more exploratory shopping experience with a scattering of bakeries, cosmetic shops, eateries, and services woven into its hallways. author: Sara Loren
html:
Jusgo Supermarket is a spacious, bright, and somewhat mysterious international market—equal parts grocery store and small-business gallery. Tucked into the same plaza as 99 Ranch Market, it offers a quieter, more exploratory shopping experience with a scattering of bakeries, cosmetic shops, eateries, and services woven into its hallways. Some areas feel vibrant and stocked, while others still feel unfinished or sparse, lending the place a wandering, almost gallery-like quality.


From fresh herbs to unusual fruits, European biscuits to frozen goods from across Asia, this spot serves as a treasure hunt for anyone who loves to cook globally. Prices vary depending on the product, but the range is undeniably broad. It’s a place you browse more than you rush through—perfect for curious cooks and casual explorers alike.


Review

Sara I. (Mar 14, 2020): 

“All is determination, To make it make sense All is determination, You can find it if you

Just let go, just let go, just, let it go" ~ Fischerspooner


"A nice, large, bright supermarket—expansive yet a bit desolate. Situated in the same plaza as 99 Ranch, Jusgo carries similar items but with its own twist. The store feels like a gallery, hosting small businesses inside: restaurants, a bakery, a bank, and cosmetic/gift shops, all lining the interior hallways.


They have an impressive selection of packaged goods, including European biscuits and chocolates displayed in ornate boxes. The produce section is lush—full of greenery, herbs, and fruits you may have never encountered. I’ve found beautiful bundles of coriander and mint here, fresh and fragrant. Great for my international cooking sprees.


Aisles hold frozen foods, dry goods, home items—honestly, you’ll find most of what you need. Prices vary. I don’t visit often, but I like dropping by for a quiet browse. The smaller shops inside, like the bakery and cosmetic store, offer warmer service. The market still feels like it's finding its footing and isn't completely finished, but if you’re here for groceries, you’ll likely leave with what you came for—and maybe a little more.”



Category: International Grocery 

Location: Sugar Land, TX

title: In-N-Out Burger – A Reliable West Coast Classic in Stafford
description: In-N-Out Burger remains one of those rare fast-food spots where simplicity truly shines—and the Stafford location captures that charm perfectly. Fast, friendly service and a straightforward menu keep things easy, while the consistently fresh ingredients make each visit reliably satisfying.The classic hamburger is the star here: a single beef patty, fresh toppings, and a toasted bun that hits every nostalgic note. Adding grilled onions and chopped peppers elevates the flavor without losing the si
author: Sara Loren
html:
In-N-Out Burger remains one of those rare fast-food spots where simplicity truly shines—and the Stafford location captures that charm perfectly. Fast, friendly service and a straightforward menu keep things easy, while the consistently fresh ingredients make each visit reliably satisfying.


The classic hamburger is the star here: a single beef patty, fresh toppings, and a toasted bun that hits every nostalgic note. Adding grilled onions and chopped peppers elevates the flavor without losing the simplicity that defines In-N-Out. While the fries are admittedly polarizing, requesting them extra crispy gives them that golden, crunchy finish many diners prefer. And for those who enjoy a twist, animal-style fries remain a cult favorite for a reason.


Shakes are thick, creamy, and nostalgic—especially when ordered Neapolitan style, a fun little secret-menu option.


Always buzzing with energy, this location brings color and movement to the Stafford area and satisfies burger cravings day and night. It’s a dependable go-to for simple, flavorful comfort—especially during the cozy months when a warm burger just feels right.


Must-Try Items:

  • Classic hamburger with grilled onions + chopped peppers

  • Fries extra crispy

  • Neapolitan shake (secret menu)

  • Animal-style fries for sauce lovers


Review

Sara I. (Oct 29, 2022): 

“This is such a great location of In and Out. Fast service and friendly folks just waiting to take your order. Menu is quite simple and easy. Food is always fresh and stellar at this location. Warm and full of flavor, considering how simple the ingredients are.


I typically just get their classic hamburger, with one beef patty and no cheese. I'll ask for grilled onions and peppers as well. The chopped peppers are great and definitely enhance the experience of this burger.

When asking for fries, I'll usually request them extra crispy so they'll have that golden flavor and crunch. Otherwise, their default fries are pale and chewy in texture. Let's face it; most people know this spot is better with their burgers and not so much their fries. Which is probably why their animal style fries are so popular, in order to mask up the flavor.


Shakes are good here as well, cold and creamy. I don't typically order those, but you can order them as neapolitan flavor as well. (secret menu)


Can't say much about this classic west coast spot. It's solid and it always delivers the random cravings for a burg. I'm glad we have one here in the Stafford area. It definitely brought a lot of light, color and movement in this part of town. Always busy and always growing. A great spot to grab a late night meal, especially in this cozy season.”



Category: Burgers, Fast Food 

Location: Stafford, Texas

title: Naha Thai Restaurant – Fresh, Fiery, and Full of Heart in Sugar Land
description: Naha Thai Restaurant brings warmth, flavor, and genuine hospitality to Sugar Land’s dining scene. Cozy, welcoming, and full of personality, this Thai eatery stands out not just for its bold dishes but also for the heartfelt conversations and charm offered by its owners. Friendly, talkative, and deeply accommodating, they make guests feel like neighbors rather than customers—an experience that lingers long after the meal ends.The food is lively, fragrant, and crafted with care. Fresh red chilies—
author: Sara Loren
html:
Naha Thai Restaurant brings warmth, flavor, and genuine hospitality to Sugar Land’s dining scene. Cozy, welcoming, and full of personality, this Thai eatery stands out not just for its bold dishes but also for the heartfelt conversations and charm offered by its owners. Friendly, talkative, and deeply accommodating, they make guests feel like neighbors rather than customers—an experience that lingers long after the meal ends.

The food is lively, fragrant, and crafted with care. Fresh red chilies—not just ground spice—give many dishes their signature punch. The pad thai is refreshingly light and crisp, leaning into a Northern Thai style that departs from the heavier, greasier versions often found elsewhere. This variation highlights brightness and texture over oiliness.


The penang curry is another standout: bubbling hot, aromatic, creamy with coconut milk, and filled with a variety of vegetables. The vegetarian version hits all the right notes, though the menu offers plenty of meat-based curries worth exploring next time. Together, these dishes showcase Naha Thai’s commitment to freshness, balance, and bold flavor.


With plans to return for soups, teas, and more, this spot easily becomes a favorite for Thai lovers in the area. An inviting setting, flavorful food, and warm conversation—Naha Thai gives Sugar Land exactly the spice and comfort it needed.


Must-Try Items:

  • Pad Thai (light, crisp & Northern Thai–inspired)

  • Penang curry (aromatic, creamy, veggie-packed)

  • Som Tum (papaya salad)

  • Any dish featuring their fresh red chilies


Review

Sara I. (Jul 26, 2022): 

“111th review! :) Naha Thai is fantastic..! From the food, to the environment, as well as the service.. there isn't much to say except that it's warm and cozy. The owners are quite friendly and talkative; it makes all the difference in the world with a chatty diner such as myself. I enjoy relishing in conversations, especially with older folk that are full of wisdom. The folks that run this place are talkative and quite accommodating.


The food is tasty and packs in a punch of heat. I love the fact that they use fresh red chilies in most of their items, instead of just ground red pepper. The pad thai here is light, fresh and crisp. Far from the typical greasy bowl types. It was nice to eat a different variation of it.. typically Northern Thai style. Every region has its own take.. but this one was refreshing.


The penang curry is great here as well. Aromatic and bubbling. The coconut milk is creamy and brimming with different veggies. I ordered the vegetarian option and found it to be delightful. Will definitely try a meat item next time and pair it with a different curry. I'm picky with curries but I can honestly say this one was the better one that I've had.


Looking forward to revisiting and trying their soups, tea + so much more. The echoes of the old restaurant that used to be here are gone. This new spot is better. I'm glad Naha is in this part of town. We needed to crank up the heat in sweet old sugar land."



Category: Thai 

Location: Sugar Land, Texas

title: Flower Child – Fresh, West Coast Spirit with Portions That Need Reviving
description: Flower Child has long been admired for bringing a vibrant, West Coast–inspired, health-forward dining experience to Houston. With its colorful bowls, sustainable ingredients, vegetarian-friendly menu, and sunny ambiance, it quickly became a favorite for those craving fresh, wholesome meals. But over the years, the experience has shifted.Where Flower Child once delivered generous portions layered with bold flavors, crisp vegetables, and nourishing grains, recent visits reveal smaller servings and
author: Sara Loren
html:
Flower Child has long been admired for bringing a vibrant, West Coast–inspired, health-forward dining experience to Houston. With its colorful bowls, sustainable ingredients, vegetarian-friendly menu, and sunny ambiance, it quickly became a favorite for those craving fresh, wholesome meals. But over the years, the experience has shifted.


Where Flower Child once delivered generous portions layered with bold flavors, crisp vegetables, and nourishing grains, recent visits reveal smaller servings and a noticeable decrease in toppings—turning bowls that once felt abundant into meals that leave diners wanting more.


Still, the menu retains its charm: forbidden rice bowls, ancient grain creations, sweet potato accents, nutritious greens, and a highly flexible lineup of vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options. The atmosphere remains bright, breezy, and uplifting, perfectly suited for a casual lunch, post-gym bite, or a feel-good dinner.


With strong potential and a loyal customer base, Flower Child continues to be a beloved spot—one that could easily return to greatness with a revival of the generous, well-balanced portions it once offered.


Highlights:

  • Vibrant, West Coast–inspired healthy bowls

  • Vegan-, vegetarian-, and gluten-free–friendly

  • Fresh ingredients, colorful presentation

  • Spacious seating & warm ambiance

  • Great variety: bowls, salads, wraps, plates, teas & more


Reviews

Sara I. Updated Review (Jul 17, 2022)

“Portions have drastically decreased at this restaurant... I ordered the mother earth bowl and only had 2 pieces of sweet potato in the bowl. I remember eating this specific item a few years ago and having more volume in the meal. They used to add more avocado and sweet potato.


Today, all I had was a measly 1 sliver of avocado and 2 chunks of sweet potato. How does anyone get full from that? Especially when it's a vegan meal to begin with... What happened Flower Child?


This restaurant was absurdly busy today, I'm assuming they're cutting corners and just not providing great meals as they used to. Everyone else enjoyed their food today; but they all agreed that it was just an ‘okay’ experience. Flower Child should consider opening up more locations. Maybe that could help.. I don't know.

All I can say is that meals should be provided with ample substance and not appear lackluster. Overpriced and it's mostly a self-serving restaurant. Fetch your own drinks and cutlery. Totally left feeling hungry.”


Sara I. Previous Review (Sep 26, 2018)

“I absolutely adore the food and the environment at Flower Child. Everything here is made fresh with a kick and snap. The menu is totally vegan friendly with a strong emphasis on using local and sustainable ingredients. There are a few meat selections that you can choose from, such as chicken, salmon, and steak. Tofu is a nice addition as well if you're into non-based meat. Thankfully, they have zero pork items here which makes me feel very comfortable.


I absolutely adore the menu; it has a strong West Coast influence and Houston was in dire need of a concept like this. It's the kind of grub that makes my belly happy and leaves me floating on cloud nine.


We visited on a cloudy Sunday afternoon, and to our surprise, the tiny line went quick and all the staff were kind and helpful. Our food didn't take long to make and was served warm and fresh.


I ordered the forbidden rice bowl with salmon as my choice of protein. I loved the savoury Asian inspired flavors that contained black pearl rice and many crisp vegetables. The mother earth is another item that I really liked. The ancient grains went very well with the sweet potatoes that were smothered in a red pepper miso vinaigrette. The broccoli pesto was vividly green and paired nicely with the leafy greens and avocado. All in all, every item danced well together in a beautiful and colorful layout.


Flower Child has salads, plates, bowls and wraps to choose from. Their drinks look great as well. I can imagine revisiting during the cooler season and wrapping around some hot tea and a warm bowl. Welcome to the city of Houston, Flower Child! I look forward to meeting you again. Until next time.”



Category: Salad, New American, Vegetarian 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston

title: Asiatown Crawl at Westcroft Center – A Cozy Cultural Food Journey
description: The Asiatown Crawl at Westcroft Center brought together warmth, culture, and good company—everything that makes a community food gathering memorable.
