With stops ranging from ice cream shops to bakeries to a specialty market, the experience was equal parts delicious and enriching.Guests enjoyed sweet treats, friendly conversations, and the chance to l
author: Sara Loren
html:
The Asiatown Crawl at Westcroft Center brought together warmth, culture, and good company—everything that makes a community food gathering memorable. This intimate event blended laughter, storytelling, and shared heritage while exploring the local gems tucked within Sharpstown’s vibrant Asiatown. With stops ranging from ice cream shops to bakeries to a specialty market, the experience was equal parts delicious and enriching.

Guests enjoyed sweet treats, friendly conversations, and the chance to learn about Middle Eastern pastries, teas, and traditions. It was a nostalgic afternoon that felt both comforting and exciting—one of those gatherings where the people make the moments just as special as the food.


Event Highlights:

  • Guided cultural insights and storytelling throughout the crawl

  • Sweet ice creams and milkshakes to kick off the experience

  • Warm, inviting bakery offering saffron tea, knafeh, butter cookies & baklava

  • Market visit with saffron, tea biscuits & regional goods

  • A cozy, laid-back gathering with friends old and new


Review

Sara I. (Jun 3, 2022): “What a cosy gathering full of my favorite people! Those are the best events—the ones where you can laugh, talk and relish with good company. No frou frou or weird vibes whatsoever. Just chill laid-back moments. Mike ended up surprising me and that made my day. Lou, as usual, was a great host.


I co-hosted a bit of the event and loved sharing the cultural background of the food as well as the local ice cream shop, bakery, and market we visited. It is my absolute pleasure to bring rich cultural heritage and perspective thrown into the mix.


We had such a great time noshing on some sweet ice cream and milkshakes. The folks at the bakery were just as warm and friendly—introducing everyone to exotic saffron tea and knafeh, which is a dessert made from Nablus cheese and shredded filo pastry. Nablus is a city in Palestine, and that is where the lovely dessert originates. I shared my knafeh with everyone and some folks grabbed butter cookies (ghraybeh) and baklava as well.


The bakery folks own the market next door and we equally enjoyed our time over there. Some friends bought saffron and others bought tea biscuits. All in all, we had a great time conversing and catching up like old times. Nostalgia at its finest mixed in with a bit of new moments. I look forward to the next event! Might be mine next time around. Cheers and syoy!”


Category: Community Events, Food Crawls 

Location: Sharpstown, Houston 


Tags: Asiatown Houston, Westcroft Center food crawl, Houston cultural events, Middle Eastern desserts Houston, Houston ice cream + bakery tour, Sharpstown community gatherings

author: Sara Loren
html:
Taizzi Sushi brings a warm, unpretentious charm to the Katy dining scene. Located in a small, busy plaza near the mall, this compact restaurant offers an unexpectedly varied menu—from sushi to Korean ramen, bibimbap, and poke bowls. Guests can choose between à la carte dining or their popular AYCE option, making it a flexible pick for anything from a quick meal to a leisurely sushi night.


Despite its tight interior, Taizzi delivers impressively attentive service, fast pacing, and a relaxed, dimly lit atmosphere that suits casual dinners. If you enjoy baked sushi, spice-forward rolls, or comforting fusion dishes, this is a welcoming spot to roll with the tides.


Must-Try Items:

  • Baked Salmon Sushi – tender, warm, and richly flavored

  • Baked Lobster Sushi – next on the list for baked-sushi lovers

  • Peppered Tuna Sashimi – bold with a satisfying kick

  • Pink Lady Roll – flavorful, balanced, and eye-catching

  • Korean Ramen & Bibimbap – hearty options beyond sushi


Reviews

Sara I. (Apr 17, 2022): 

“Roll with the tides! Taizzi Sushi in Katy isn't too far from the local mall. Decided to stop by on a whim with a good friend for dinner. I thought the food here was pretty decent. They've got quite a large selection of grub to choose from the menu. I spotted Korean style ramen, bibimbap, and even poke bowls on the menu. This spot is known for their AYCE selection or just wing it a la carte.


Settled in for sushi because that's what this place is known for. First of all, the plaza is tiny and the restaurant is cramped as well. Surprisingly though on a Saturday night, we found decent parking and it wasn't too busy inside—most likely due to the holidays.


Service was impeccable. Since it’s a small space, the servers continuously checked up on us. One of them even offered me a fork since I'm not the biggest fan of using chopsticks. Lol.


My favorite item was the baked sushi. I've always been a fan of baked sushi and they've got a decent selection. The baked salmon sushi we ordered was tender and flavorful. Definitely want to try the baked lobster option next time. Runner up was the peppered tuna sashimi and the Pink Lady sushi—both had a bite and a kick to them.


The jasmine tea wasn't that good though; flat and lukewarm. The interior is dark and cozy, good for a dinner vibe. They've got a TV inside blasting Korean music to keep you awake with all the glutinous rice intake. Wouldn’t mind revisiting when around the area—especially after shopping and settling in for cozy starch bombs. That's what sushi is after all, am I right? Lol. Keep it local & prosper! Until next time. :)”

Sara I. (Mar 16, 2019):

author: Sara Loren
html:
Buc-ee’s in Richmond may be one of the smaller outposts of the iconic Texas chain, but it still delivers the charm, convenience, and quick-stop satisfaction locals adore. This location is built for speedy in-and-out visits—perfect for grabbing a hot drink, stocking up on road-trip snacks, or fueling up before heading back toward Sugar Land or the surrounding areas.


Despite its compact size, the essentials are all here: hot coffee, cold bottled drinks, deli bites, baked goods, and everyday necessities like milk and eggs. The attached gas station and car wash make it a reliable one-stop shop, even if it doesn’t boast the massive retail section found in their flagship stores.


Must-Try / Must-Grab Items

  • Piping hot Buc-ee’s coffee (strong & smooth)

  • Banana pudding cups

  • Fresh deli snacks & baked goods

  • Assorted cold bottled beverages

  • Quick-access essentials (milk, eggs, grab-and-go treats)


Review

Sara I. (Feb 4, 2022): 

“This is just a simple and quick grab n’ go Buc-ee’s. If you're randomly craving their in-store snacks and treats, you'll find that here. They have the usual assortment of hot coffee, deli items and baked goods. I like their coffee—strong, piping hot, and far from bitter.


Granted, this location is much smaller than their other storefronts, but many of their products are still available. It has fewer bells and whistles though; for souvenirs or gifts, you’ll need to visit a larger Buc-ee’s. This one has an attached gas station and car wash just like the others. I’ve heard good things about their car wash, so I’ll definitely revisit.


I grabbed my favorite banana pudding and some coffee. Service was quick and simple. With plenty of beverages and random necessities like milk and eggs, it’s a handy little spot not far from Sugar Land. Parking is a bit tight, but again, this is totally a grab-and-go location. Toodle-oo!”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Sugar Land Memorial Park offers a peaceful retreat tucked just far enough from the bustle of daily life. With still, glasslike water winding through its landscape and wide open spaces ideal for walking, fishing, or simply breathing deeply, this park is a serene gem within the suburbs. Winter and spring highlight its beauty even more—cool air, soft sunlight, and the quiet hum of nature set the mood for rest or reflection.


Whether you're bringing friends, family, or furry companions, the spacious grounds and minimal traffic noise make it easy to unwind. The park features a large pavilion near the entrance for gatherings, scenic paths stretching into grassy fields, and occasional closed-off areas near the memorial obelisk. Despite that, there’s plenty of room to roam, move, and reconnect with nature.


What to Enjoy at Sugar Land Memorial Park

  • Tranquil water views perfect for fishing or quiet contemplation

  • Long concrete walking paths ideal for exercise

  • Unique trees and local bird sightings

  • A spacious pavilion for gatherings

  • Peaceful, low-noise environment for strolling or relaxing


Review

Sara I. (Jan 21, 2022): 

“Calm. Clean. Crystal clear. I'm describing this park and the water that stretches throughout the land it's situated on. Very peaceful. You can go fishing near the water or just reflect upon life. I hope you do enough reflections and meditation—maybe this park will inspire you to do just that.


I love visiting this quiet and tucked-away park in the winter and spring seasons. Bring your friends, doggie pals, and family. You don't hear too much traffic noise, especially as you wander far off into the grass. There are a few unique trees and birds here as well.


At the front of the entrance you'll find a cosy yet large pavilion for gatherings and picnics. There's a small section of the park closed for now (near the memorial obelisk). Other than that, there's plenty of concrete to stretch your legs and walk upon. Keep moving. That's always the goal. You'll find that here.”



Category: Parks 

Location: Sugar Land, TX

Review

Sara I. (Nov 30, 2021): 

“I hadn’t visited this location in years. It’s tucked into a large shopping plaza in a busy part of Stafford—one I used to frequent over a decade ago when this was a Cold Stone Creamery. This Marble Slab is just OK. The servers were friendly and let me try a few samples, but many flavors tasted quite artificial, which is expected for a large chain. title: Brasil – A Montrose Classic with Room to Improve
description: Brasil has been a longstanding neighborhood fixture in Montrose—casual, artsy, and effortlessly cool in that old-school Houston way. author: Sara Loren
html:
Brasil has been a longstanding neighborhood fixture in Montrose—casual, artsy, and effortlessly cool in that old-school Houston way. The café blends coffeehouse culture with a diverse, globally inspired menu, offering everything from pizzas and tamales to soups, pastries, and vegan-friendly fare. Whether you sit on the breezy patio or inside the dim, relaxed dining area, the ambiance is nostalgic and unfussy.


That said, service quality seems to vary, and billing issues have been noted—making it important for guests to double-check receipts and remain aware during checkout. When Brasil is at its best, it’s comforting, flavorful, and quintessentially Montrose; but consistency in customer care would elevate the experience significantly.


Review

Sara I. (Jan 21, 2020):

 “I’ve been visiting this café for well over a decade and things really haven’t changed much. I recently visited twice, thinking the service was top-notch. After getting home and discovering they charged us for food we never ordered, my thoughts changed immediately. Management was sneaky and fraudulent. I don’t know why they’d have the audacity to charge customers for items they didn’t order. It’s a nuisance to revisit the café just to find out what happened. Be careful—ask for a receipt and make sure they don’t swipe your card twice.


I’ve always enjoyed the pizzas and tamales here. The soups are not bad, and there are many vegetarian and vegan options, which is a plus. Their café au lait is one of my favorites, served in a tall glass just like in European cafés. I always ask for maple syrup—it makes the drink feel even cozier. Sitting outside on the patio in good weather or inside the dim café is equally nice. The atmosphere appeals to me because it feels casual yet chic. It’s one of the originals in this part of town—no try-hard factor. Lots of diverse food and drink options; it’s a quick choice that keeps your belly warm and full. I just hope they can improve in terms of service.”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Category: International Grocery 

Location: Westchase, Houston 


Seiwa Market is a tidy, well-organized specialty grocer focused entirely on Japanese products. Though smaller in size, the shelves are packed with unique imported items—from sauces and pantry staples to snacks, drinks, and specialty treats you won’t find in mainstream grocery stores. Prices can be steep due to import costs, but the selection appeals to anyone who enjoys niche Japanese ingredients or likes exploring international markets.


What to Expect

  • Spotless aisles and a compact but curated selection

  • Japanese pantry staples including Kewpie mayo, dressings, sauces, and snacks

  • Hit-or-miss produce, though the store keeps everything neatly displayed

  • Ready-to-drink beverages like canned coffees, teas, and tapioca drinks

  • A small fresh-food section, typically minimal depending on time of day


Must-Try Items

  • Bourbon chocolate biscuits – crisp, rich, and addictive

  • Wasabi rice crackers

  • Sangaria Royal Milk Tea – clean, lightly sweet, simple ingredients

  • Japanese pantry staples (Kewpie mayo, dressings, curry mixes, sauces)


Review

Sara I. (Nov 4, 2021):

 “I like this market! It’s a small specialty shop with exclusively Japanese products. Always clean, always organized, and never overly scented. The produce is hit or miss—cilantro was limp, but cherry tomatoes were vibrant. Prices can be a shock, especially for imported dressings and sauces.


The fresh food section was pretty bare when I visited, though I’m not sure I’d buy sushi here anyway. I love their chocolate bourbon biscuits—crisp and very chocolatey—as well as their savory rice crackers. I picked up wasabi ones this time. They carry plenty of ready-to-drink coffees and teas; my favorite is Sangaria Royal Milk Tea, lightly sweet and made with simple ingredients.


This plaza is quiet and tucked away, but worth the stop if you like browsing international markets. Support local!”



Tags: Seiwa Market Houston, Japanese grocery Houston, Westchase international markets, Japanese snacks Houston, Sangaria Royal Milk Tea, kewpie mayo Houston

Ding Tea offers milk teas, lattes, juices, and yogurt-based Yakult drinks, all perfect for our mostly warm seasons.


The tapioca is firm and chewy, not too sweet, and pairs beautifully with the honey milk tea. I like their rounded serving cups too—smaller and easier to sip without feeling overly full. I always ask for half ice and half sweetened, and they got it just right. Service was friendly and quick. Ding Tea is pretty popular across the U.S., and I can see why. I’ll definitely drop by again to try more items off the menu. But when in doubt, choose the classic milk tea!”

Lava Coffee delivers exactly what you want from a neighborhood café: warmth, personality, and thoughtfully crafted drinks. With its industrial–European blend of décor, glowing ambient bulbs, and plush seating, this Katy hideaway feels both stylish and comforting. It’s an ideal mid-afternoon stop after wandering through Katy Mills or exploring Katy Asian Town, offering signature lattes and a focused menu of pastries to pair with them.


The standout here is the hospitality—Sasha, the owner, brings genuine care and enthusiasm to each drink, making the space feel welcoming and personal. Locally sourced beans, balanced flavors, and a calm environment make Lava Coffee a spot worth seeking out whenever you’re in the area.


Review

Sara I. (Jan 1, 2020): 

“I’m loving the warm industrial-meets-European décor here—soft lights, cozy chairs, and a posh vibe tucked quietly within Katy Asia Town. Stopped in after shopping at Katy Mills, and it ended up being the perfect afternoon pick-me-up.


Sasha, the owner, was incredibly friendly and made me the Honey Bear Latte (honey, vanilla, cinnamon). I ordered it iced but received it hot instead; Sasha offered to remake it, but honestly, I’m glad the mix-up happened. The hot version was creamy, soothing, and wonderful. I can imagine the iced one would be just as good. Their signature drinks look great, and the tea selection is extensive.


The beans are locally sourced, aromatic, and comforting, and although the pastry case is small, the drinks are clearly the star. If this café were closer, I’d be here much more often. Worth the trip whenever you’re in the area. Support local whenever you can!”

title: Black Bear Diner – A Cozy, Woodsy Sugar Land Staple with NorCal Charm
description: Black Bear Diner in Sugar Land wraps guests in a warm, nostalgic embrace—bringing the forested charm of Northern California straight into Texas. With its woodsy décor, whimsical bear accents, and comforting diner energy, it feels like stepping inside a storybook lodge. Since opening in 2019, this spot has become a beloved local go-to for families, brunch groups, and anyone craving hearty comfort food served with genuine hospitality.The menu is extensive, offering everything from savory breakfast
author: Sara Loren
html:
Black Bear Diner in Sugar Land wraps guests in a warm, nostalgic embrace—bringing the forested charm of Northern California straight into Texas. With its woodsy décor, whimsical bear accents, and comforting diner energy, it feels like stepping inside a storybook lodge. Since opening in 2019, this spot has become a beloved local go-to for families, brunch groups, and anyone craving hearty comfort food served with genuine hospitality.

The menu is extensive, offering everything from savory breakfast plates to sweet treats and classic diner staples. Service is consistently warm, even during high-traffic weekends when crowds spill out the door. Though the food can occasionally be hit-or-miss during busy waves, the overall experience remains cozy, familiar, and cherished by many.


Must-Try Items:

  • Patty melt (on a good day, savory and classic)

  • Warm, tender pancakes

  • Omelets & hot breakfast plates

  • Sweet, creamy hot chocolate

  • Desserts & comforting diner sides


Review

Sara I. (Jan 16, 2024): 

“BBD... aka Black Bear Diner.. such a cozy spot that reminds me of GoldiLocks and the three bears... except this bear theme is originating from Nor'Cal. Hence the theme of alll the northern trees and Nor'Cal Diner Vibes.. and yes.. some of my favorite diners are in California (my HomeState).


On with the food. This spot has been tucked away within the land of Sugar since 2019.. I've been visiting since then and have always enjoyed the grub at BBD. Albeit, there are some days when the food’s perfectly on par, and then on some days when it's just okay.


Within my most recent visit... lines were out the door, frigid air was kickin' in and groups of folks were simmering within the cozy diner. Thankfully a group of us were seated promptly and found good seats closer to the entrance. Due to the fact they were busy.. it seemed the food was just okay this time. I ordered a beef patty melt with fries and coleslaw. Fries were blonde in color, cold, and such few. Patty melt was okay. Pancakes were warm and tender as they typically are. With such a huge crowd on the weekends, food can be subpar at times.


Other than that, I have always appreciated BBD's expansive menu. Their hot chocolate is sweet, warm and creamy, and their desserts are quite nice as well. Savory hot items such as their omelets and other sandwiches are typically good.


Dining experience and service? Great. BBD has a nostalgic, woodsy, Nor'Cal feel that will make any nature enthusiast appreciative of their whimsical theme of all things bears and forests. They even sell a few bear plushies, socks, and all cuddlesy stuff at the front (where you pay). Service has always been warm and appreciative. Servers almost always check up on you. Though, they ought to put table numbers or order numbers on the table. At least twice during the weekend rush they brought out wrong food orders to our table.

All in all, this is a spot that many cherish. Perf for families, friends and groups of folk that wanna chat over coffee, pancakes and all the sweeter things in life. Until next time!”



Category: Breakfast & Brunch, American, Diners 

Location: Sugar Land, TX 


Tags: Black Bear Diner Sugar Land, best diners Houston suburbs, NorCal diner vibes Texas, family brunch Sugar Land, cozy breakfast spots Houston, classic American comfort food

title: Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy – Vegan Comfort Meets Global Flavor
description: Tucked into a calm corner of Sugar Creek Plaza, Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy brings warmth, creativity, and a global twist to Sugar Land’s dining scene. With its soothing ambiance, friendly service, and unexpectedly diverse vegan menu, this spot welcomes everyone—from full-time vegans to anyone who enjoys fresh, vibrant, plant-forward meals.The menu is impressively varied, offering pizzas, soups, salads, and even Persian-inspired dishes that celebrate bold, comforting flavors. It’s the k
author: Sara Loren
html:
Tucked into a calm corner of Sugar Creek Plaza, Pythagoras Conscious Food Philosophy brings warmth, creativity, and a global twist to Sugar Land’s dining scene. With its soothing ambiance, friendly service, and unexpectedly diverse vegan menu, this spot welcomes everyone—from full-time vegans to anyone who enjoys fresh, vibrant, plant-forward meals.


The menu is impressively varied, offering pizzas, soups, salads, and even Persian-inspired dishes that celebrate bold, comforting flavors. It’s the kind of place where you can settle in with friends, share a colorful spread, and leave feeling both nourished and pleasantly full.


Whether you're exploring vegan cuisine or seeking a cozy neighborhood hangout with thoughtful food, Pythagoras proves that plant-based dining can be soulful, satisfying, and deeply delicious.


What to Try:

  • Loaded vegan nachos with crisp toppings & flavorful vegan cheese

  • Sesame bread served with Persian-style eggplant dip

  • Crispy-crust pizzas with generous toppings & surprisingly delicious vegan cheese

  • Grapefruit sparkling drink or fresh juices


Review

Sara I. (Jul 6, 2022):

“Such a cozy little spot! I'm liking this conscious food philosophy on a quiet yet nonchalant corner of Sugar Creek plaza. I've always liked this little part of town and Pythagoras vegan cafe is a warm and bright welcome in the area. I met up with friends this evening and we all enjoyed our meals.


Despite the menu being primarily of vegan food choices; there really is something for everyone here. The menu is chock full of pizza choices, soups, salads and Persian food items. We started with their loaded vegan nachos as an appetizer and it was quite filling and crisp. Plenty of veggies and the vegan cheese doused on top had a good flavor. Nachos were light and a great sharing item with friends.


I'm not vegan but I enjoy eating fresh vegan and vegetarian foods as often as possible. I love the fresh breads here; such as their sesame bread that comes with their Persian style eggplant dip. Delish. As well as their pizzas; the crust is crispy and the toppings are generous. I'm typically not a fan of vegan cheese, but theirs is quite good.


I recommend their grapefruit sparkling drink (non-alcoholic) or their juices. It's great to have a new vegan food joint in the area. The theme of the restaurant is unique and their service was warm and efficient. Our waiter was friendly, communicative and often checked up on us.


Thanks dear Pythagoras for enlightening our minds on a random summer evening. It's just simple Pythagorean math; our bellies were full and our hearts felt warm. What more would you want?”



Category: Vegan, Pizza, Cocktail Bars 

Location: Sugar Land, TX 


Tags: vegan restaurants Sugar Land, plant-based dining Houston suburbs, vegan pizza Houston, Persian vegan food, healthy eats Sugar Land, Pythagoras restaurant review

author: Sara Loren
html:
Category: Antiques

Market Place Antiques & Collectibles is a sprawling, delightfully dusty treasure hunt tucked into Spring Branch—a warehouse-style maze of booths, vendors, and relics from eras long gone. Whether you're a seasoned antiquer or simply someone who appreciates a stroll through history, this spot offers a nostalgic and eclectic way to spend a weekend afternoon. With items ranging from ornate grandfather clocks to delicate teacup sets, the marketplace leans into its vintage charm and invites you to slow down, browse, and imagine the stories behind each piece.


What You’ll Find

  • Grandfather clocks, old-world vases, oil paintings

  • Vintage tea sets and post-Victorian–style decor

  • Antique wooden furniture, including ottomans and dresser cabinets

  • Vendor booths with personable sellers and curated finds


The space is dusty, eccentric, and full of personality—exactly what you’d expect from a longstanding antique hub. Even if you don’t buy anything, the experience itself is worth the visit.


Review

Sara I. (Oct 25, 2021): 

“Decent and quite a large marketplace to explore on a random weekend afternoon. I’m not an ‘antiquer,’ but it’s nice to visit old spots like this that take you down memory lane—albeit many of the items here are way before my time. They have super old grandfather clocks, vases, paintings, etc., from eras gone by. It’s dusty and eccentric as you sprawl through the warehouse.


There are a few vendors with their own little setups, and many are talkative—ready to suggest items that might appeal to you. I haven’t bought anything yet, but the wooden furniture caught my eye, especially the ottoman tables and dresser cabinets. The vintage teacup sets were dainty and charming as well.


Many items aren’t things you particularly need, but it’s still lovely to appreciate vintage craftsmanship—things were built to last back then. I recommend visiting on a cozy weekend afternoon. They’re only open Fri–Sun anyway. Rain or shine, most likely.”



Tags: Houston antique shops, Spring Branch vintage stores, antique furniture Houston, collectibles market Houston, weekend antiquing HTX

title: Koreatown HTX Meetup: Shabu & Market Tour
description: The Koreatown HTX Foodie Adventure brought together friends, flavor, and cultural exploration in one seamlessly organized event. Focused on Korean cuisine and ending with a lively wander through HMart, this meetup blended education, great food, and community bonding into a memorable Sunday experience.The highlight of the outing was a delicious Shabu-style meal—vegetarian for some, seafood and meat options for others—all seasoned with the bold sauces, spices, and banchan that define comforting Ko
author: Sara Loren
html:
The Koreatown HTX Foodie Adventure brought together friends, flavor, and cultural exploration in one seamlessly organized event. Focused on Korean cuisine and ending with a lively wander through HMart, this meetup blended education, great food, and community bonding into a memorable Sunday experience.


The highlight of the outing was a delicious Shabu-style meal—vegetarian for some, seafood and meat options for others—all seasoned with the bold sauces, spices, and banchan that define comforting Korean cooking. Each guest had their own personal hot pot setup, complete with adjustable heat controls, making the meal both engaging and customizable. Service was attentive throughout, creating a smooth, enjoyable dining experience.

After the meal, a group shopping adventure through HMart added an extra layer of fun. From rambutan to fresh nectarines to unique pantry items, everyone found something to spark curiosity. The outing wrapped with goodie bags, laughter, and the joy of reconnecting with familiar faces.


Event Highlights:

  • Personalized Shabu hot pot with vegetarian, seafood & meat options

  • Flavorful sauces, banchan & herbs

  • Attentive service and smooth event hosting

  • Post-meal grocery exploration at HMart

  • Fun finds: rambutan, nectarines & specialty items

  • Catching up with beloved community members

  • A cozy, flavorful, community-centered Sunday


Review

Sara I. (Aug 27, 2023):

“What a wonderful event. All things Korean food and stopping at HMART as the last part of the adventure tour! I remember when Shabu style food was mentioned — I was already intrigued from the get-go. Because of it having a Korean flair I knew that I would enjoy the food, simply because of the sauces, spice and many different condiments (banchan) veggies and herbs. That is what I got here as I inhaled my vegetarian style shabu and my friends equally enjoyed their meal as well. They have seafood and meat options as well and everyone dug in and went back for more for this AYCE style concept.


Service was attentive and everything was well taken care of. I got to learn a few new techniques in regards to Shabu and hot soup dining. I like this style as it's not a communal pot that you all dig out of. You can adjust the temperature of your soup as well or just turn it off, all with a remote on the side of the table.

A few of us ventured off to HMart afterwards in search of more unique goodies. We purchased rambutan, fresh nectarine and a few shelf items. It was fun exploring the grocery store on a very crowded Sunday.

It was great catching up with a few old school friends while munching on hot soup. Good seeing Victoria, Tabatha and Genae as well. Thank y'all for your humor, silliness and good company. Cheers and SYOY until next time!”



Category: Cultural Food Events, Community Meetups 

Location: Spring Branch, Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
Roast & Brew brings a refreshing, airy charm to the Heights—a café designed for comfort, conversation, and creativity. Filled with windows, natural light, and plenty of workspace seating, it’s the kind of spot where you can settle in with a book, meet friends, or enjoy a quiet morning ritual. With evening hours stretching until midnight, it’s also one of Houston’s rare late-night coffeehouse gems.


The menu leans modern European with a Greek twist—pastries, chocolates, and light bites that pair beautifully with their rich coffee and fragrant teas. Whether you're craving an Americano, a warm pastry, or a sunny place to unwind, this shop consistently delivers warmth without the pretense.


What to Try

  • Americano – bold, robust, and beautifully extracted

  • Blueberry muffin – tender, lightly sweet, and freshly baked

  • Greek chocolates – unique treats you won’t find in most Houston cafés

  • Hot teas & herbal options – aromatic and soothing


Review

Sara I. (Oct 13, 2021):

“Roast and Brew is such a stellar coffee shop! I love the open-air seating and bright natural light pouring through the windows. There’s plenty of space inside, many tables with outlets, and a front patio if you prefer sitting outdoors. It’s a great spot for socializing or studying—calm, ambient music and never too loud.


The menu is lovely. I’ve had their teas, coffee, and the blueberry muffin, which was tender, fresh, and slightly sweet—perfect with a strong Americano. They also carry Greek chocolates, some of my favorites!


The staff is warm and attentive, and I love that they now stay open until midnight. The vibes are comfortable, easygoing, and completely unpretentious. I’ll continue supporting this local gem whenever I’m in the Heights. Until next time!”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Verbena Coffee is a warm, wood-toned retreat tucked into the Memorial/Energy Corridor area—a neighborhood café that has quickly grown into a beloved local staple. With Scandinavian-inspired interiors, thoughtfully crafted drinks, and collaborations with nearby bakeries and pop-ups, it’s the kind of space that invites you to slow down on a rainy morning or tuck in for a cozy afternoon recharge.


The drink menu leans comforting and aromatic, featuring house-made syrups, quality loose-leaf teas, and espresso beverages that highlight balance over excess sweetness. Whether you're a coffee devotee or a tea enthusiast, Verbena offers something crafted with intention.


What to Try

  • London Fog Latte – loose-leaf Earl Grey steeped in foamy milk with fragrant vanilla

  • Brown Sugar Latte – lightly sweet, house-made syrup; add cinnamon for extra warmth

  • Cappuccino – classic, well-balanced, and smooth

  • Local loaf cakes & croissants – baked goods delivered fresh from nearby partners


Review

Sara I. (May 23, 2021): 

“Such a great little coffee shop in the neighborhood, and it hasn’t even been open for two years. They’re thriving in the Memorial area and it’s wonderful supporting local. I love visiting independently owned coffee shoppes and trying the drinks they craft in house.


My favorite here is the London Fog latte—close to my heart, and not everyone makes it right. Their loose-leaf Earl Grey steeped in warm, foamy milk with fragrant vanilla is perfect. The bergamot is sharp and comforting, especially on a gray and rainy day.


Coffee drinks are just as good. The brown sugar latte, made with their house syrup, isn’t overly sweet—adding cinnamon makes the flavor pop. Cappuccinos are solid too. I’m looking forward to trying their sliced loaf cakes and croissants from a local bakery.


The interior is woodsy and tan, very Scandinavian. They also host pop-ups with other cafés like Koffeteria. Always something fun happening at this neighborhood spot. Until next time.”

While dine-in may be limited, their to-go dumplings travel well and arrive piping hot, making this an easy go-to for a cozy night in.Beyond dumplings, you’ll find crisp scallion pancakes, simple sauces, and a menu
author: Sara Loren
html:
Golden Dumpling House is the definition of a hidden gem—small, unassuming, and deeply rooted in the craft of traditional dumpling-making. Their offerings lean classic and comforting: thick, chewy wrappers, generously packed fillings, and that signature burst of steam when you bite in. While dine-in may be limited, their to-go dumplings travel well and arrive piping hot, making this an easy go-to for a cozy night in.


Beyond dumplings, you’ll find crisp scallion pancakes, simple sauces, and a menu of home-style dishes that reflect a no-frills, flavor-first approach. Cash-only, but worth every penny.


Must-Try Items

  • Steamed Chicken Dumplings – tender filling wrapped in chewy, old-world–style dough

  • Pan-Fried Beef Dumplings – crisp bottoms, juicy interior, deeply savory

  • Scallion Pancakes – house-made, crispy, and far superior to frozen versions

  • Black Vinegar Dumpling Sauce – the best complement to the hearty fillings


Review

Sara I. (Apr 29, 2021): 

“Golden Dumpling House seems to serve up some rather mean—actually, cute and authentic—dumplings. They’re doughy, chewy, and filled to the brim. Inside each dumpling is a hefty meatball-like center brimming with flavor. The texture is very old world, and they are super boiling hot when you nosh on them. Fresh at its best.


My favorites are the steamed chicken dumplings and the pan-fried beef dumplings—sealed with flavor and great texture. The chili sauce has way too much oil and not enough heat, but the black vinegar sauce is solid. I do wish they offered a plain shrimp and chive dumpling since not everyone eats pork; seafood dumplings would be a great addition.


The scallion pancakes are crispy and clearly house-made—nothing like the flat freezer versions you find elsewhere. Orders take about 20–25 minutes to prepare, so call ahead, and make sure to order by 7:30 pm if you’re picking up in the evening. Service was chill and prompt. Cash only.


They’ve got plenty on the menu besides dumplings, and I’ll definitely revisit to try more. Support local mom-and-pop shops—these folks put soul into their craft.”


Category: Chinese 

Location: Chinatown, Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
[MOVED LOCATIONS - From Galleria to Montrose]


Yummy’s Hot Chicken takes the ever-popular hot chicken trend and elevates it with a bold Syrian twist. This unassuming food truck delivers layers of flavor, crunch, and spice that set it apart from the typical fried-chicken lineup. The menu may be small, but each item is crafted with intention—crispy textures, vibrant toppings, and spice levels that range from gentle heat to full-on fire.


The chicken stays remarkably juicy beneath its golden crust, and the bright slaw adds a refreshing snap that balances the richness. Fans of creative comfort food will appreciate the unique touches, including Middle Eastern-inspired seasoning blends and their standout curry fries. Grab your order early, especially in hot weather—the food is worth savoring before the Houston heat kicks in.


Must-Try Items

  • Syrian Hot Chicken Sandwich (medium spice recommended) – crisp, fresh, full of layered flavor

  • Curry Fries – fragrant curry sauce blended with cheese; hot, bold, and delicious

  • Chicken Tender Basket – same addictive seasoning in tender form

  • Challah Bun Option – soft, slightly sweet, and a perfect match for the heat


Review

Sara I. (Aug 16, 2020): 

“Hot. Crispy. Chicken sandwich. But with a Syrian twist.

This sandwich was hecka good—lots of flavor, layers, and textures. Yummy’s has a small, simple menu, but every item overdelivers. I rarely eat anything fried, but their unique twist puts this sandwich in a league of its own. The slaw is bright and vibrant, and the chicken crust is crisp and golden.


They offer different spice levels; I chose medium and it was just right. The curry fries were surprisingly delicious—an interesting fusion with curry sauce meshed into mild cheese sauce, and they arrived steaming hot. My sandwich came on a challah bun instead of a pretzel bun, and I loved it. Definitely ask which bun they’re using.

Everything was crisp and yummy. This spot packs heat and taste. I’ll probably revisit in the fall—eating outside in summer was an adventure in itself! Thanks, Yummy’s. Hope y’all continue to thrive in the Galleria food truck park.”



Category: Food Trucks, Chicken Shop, Sandwiches 

Location: Montrose, Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
World Market in Stafford offers a vibrant, culturally rich escape—perfect for anyone who thrives on global flavors, décor, and eclectic treasures. Though smaller than the long-established Post Oak location, this newer store still brings an impressive spread of international goods, pantry staples, and uniquely crafted home items. From European chocolates to Middle Eastern spices, from artisan mugs to bright textiles, the store feels like a tiny world tour tucked inside the suburbs.


Service is warm, the ambiance is cozy, and the aisles are full of delightful surprises—halal gummy candies, curated teas, candles, cookware, pottery, and seasonal imports that keep each visit fresh. For anyone craving the joy of travel during quiet seasons or limited movement, this shop becomes an unexpected comfort.


Must-Try Picks

  • German marzipan chocolate

  • British & international teas

  • Halal gummy candies

  • Global spices & pantry goods

  • Candles, pottery, and unique ceramic bowls


Review

Sara I. (Jul 21, 2020): 

“It is wonderful to explore this culturally diverse store during limited moments of traveling. Anything cultural and world related excites the heck out of me. Thank y’all for opening this store during such obscure times.


World Market has always been a favorite of mine—we had a Sugar Land location over a decade ago, where I’d grab all my culinary staples. It closed long ago, so having one in Stafford now, just minutes from Sugar Land, is such a treat.


This location feels smaller than the Post Oak one, but there’s still so much to browse: candles, spices, halal gummy candies, chocolate (the German marzipan is my favorite!), and a lovely selection of British and international teas. The mugs, bowls, and pottery are beautiful as well.


If you’re into cultural and global goods like I am, you’ll dig this store. It’s my home away from home. Good service and warm ambiance. When the travel bug bites, I make my way to World Market. Until next time. Adeus!”

Review

Sara I. (Apr 3, 2020): 

“I’m normally not a fan of monster-like donuts—the custom ones loaded with crazy ingredients. Fun to look at, creative even, but taste-wise? Meh. I’m a simple donut gal. Give me a chocolate-glazed, a sprinkle donut, or a soft cinnamon twist and I’m happy.


The cinnamon twists here are my absolute favorite—soft, stretchy, yeast-like, and just lightly glazed. The Homer donut with pink frosting and sprinkles is another sweet treat; the subtle strawberry flavor is cute and nostalgic. The custom French toast donut, though? Hit or miss. My recent trip was a total miss. The whipped cream melted instantly, and the whole thing tasted overwhelmingly of batter—soggy and unimpressive. Their Instagram photos look incredible, so it’s disappointing when the real thing doesn’t match.


On a brighter note, the lemon jelly donut was yummy, and the coffee was fresh, hot, and strong. They offer savory items like fusion tacos, sandwiches, kolaches, and croissants—honestly, I think their savory creativity fares better than their sweet experiments.


This spot is still a fun little pick-me-up in the middle of sleepy Richmond. A great place for a classic donut and coffee. Support local, enjoy something simple, and wash those hands. ;)”



Category: Donuts, Delis, Cafes 

Location: Richmond, TX 


Tags: Richmond TX donuts, custom donuts Houston area, cinnamon twist donuts, local donut shops Texas, deli & donuts Richmond, coffee and donuts Richmond

author: Sara Loren
html:
Koffeteria brings an artistic, vintage charm to EaDo—a neighborhood known for its creative energy and urban edge. With its antique cupboards, quirky décor, and inventive pastry case, this café stands out as a destination for those who love personality in their coffee shops. Whether you're stopping in before exploring downtown or grabbing a treat on the go, Koffeteria offers a mix of bold flavors and nostalgic ambiance.


While service can fluctuate depending on the time of day, the café still draws visitors for its refreshing beverages, imaginative baked goods, and distinctive, old-world interior. It's a spot worth returning to, especially earlier in the day, to catch their most famous pastries at their freshest.


Must-Try Items:

  • Iced Latte (refreshing, milky, lightly balanced)

  • Herbal Iced Tea (flavorful + lightly sweetened)

  • Thick & Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookie

  • Eclectic Croissants (not yet tried, but highly talked about!)


Review

Sara I. (Jun 5, 2022): “Unique and vintage coffee shoppe within the EaDo district of Houston. This part of town isn't too far off from the novelty of hanging out, or heading towards downtown htx. Just dropped by for a little bit as I was headed towards discovery green for a venture in the park.


My friend and I entered about 30 minutes before closing. The staff was as stiff as cardboard. No warmth or anything. We decided upon cold bevvies as it was a warm day out in the city. They made me a simple iced latte, which was refreshing and milky. Not too strong. Just good. My friend enjoyed his herbal iced tea which was packed with flavor and was lightly sweetened.


We also grabbed their thick and chewy chocolate chip cookie. It was delicious and buttery. Not entirely sure how the other pastries would fare but they certainly looked tasty.


I loved the antique interior—the cupboard, cabinets, and little trinkets. The coffee table was dirty though and so was the floor around where we sat. Staff might have gotten busy since they were 30 mins til closing.


A little hyped. May visit earlier next time around and grab a different bevvie. Have heard quite a lot about their eclectic croissants. I'm not usually in the EaDo district of town, as it's a bit ways out. Definitely an urban exploration, but will certainly revisit when given the chance.”

title: Terry Hershey Park – A Wooded Escape in the Energy Corridor
description: Terry Hershey Park is one of Houston’s most beloved green escapes—an expansive, tree-lined sanctuary tucked right into the bustle of the Energy Corridor. With multiple entrances that each lead to different winding paths, bridges, and leafy tunnels, the park feels both vast and intimate, offering something for walkers, runners, bicyclists, and nature lovers alike.Its long corridors of trees create shaded pathways that stretch for miles, making it easy to get wonderfully lost in the scenery. Hidde
author: Sara Loren
html:
Terry Hershey Park is one of Houston’s most beloved green escapes—an expansive, tree-lined sanctuary tucked right into the bustle of the Energy Corridor. With multiple entrances that each lead to different winding paths, bridges, and leafy tunnels, the park feels both vast and intimate, offering something for walkers, runners, bicyclists, and nature lovers alike.


Its long corridors of trees create shaded pathways that stretch for miles, making it easy to get wonderfully lost in the scenery. Hidden pockets of charm appear throughout the park, from neighborhood-adjacent corners to community-decorated benches and even a tiny outdoor library where visitors can borrow or leave a book. Seasonal beauty shines here—especially in spring and autumn, when wildflowers glow and cooler air turns afternoon walks into something magical.


Whether you're seeking movement, fresh air, or a peaceful reset, Terry Hershey Park remains a treasured reminder of nature’s resilience within Houston’s “concrete jungle.”


Must-Enjoy Experiences:

  • Long, winding tree-canopied trails

  • Bridges connecting different sections of the park

  • Jogging, cycling & long-distance walking corridors

  • Hidden neighborhood corners with charming touches (like a mini library!)

  • Seasonal scenery—especially spring wildflowers and autumn strolls


Reviews

Sara I. (May 25, 2022): “A rather large yet cozy park smacked in the middle of the energy corridor. There are various entrances to reach this park; & yet each entrance happens to guide you through a unique path. I love the large stretched out corridors here. These are tunnels that are full of trees that stretch so far out into various pathways and bridges. Great for those that are joggers or bicyclists. I find myself mostly walking here and yet I can't seem to finish the trail. It's easy to get lost here as well. Lol. Unless you spot a map or something.


As mentioned, the trails are long and unwinding. I had always known about this park yet its entrances were mysterious, and easily missed. Frequently visiting and being near the beltway, I was able to spot one of the main entrances and that was it. I've been a frequent stroller here for the past 2 years.


This park seems to have been here forever; I hope it stays & that it continues to preserve itself within the midst of the concrete jungle. There are vast neighborhoods tucked within the corners of some of the pathways. One of the neighbors decorated a bench and left a mini library outside so walkers can grab books & leave a book as well. It's these little things that are precious & that have made this park ever so charming.


I love visiting in Autumn and Spring in particular. Last year I spotted a field of yellow flowers. Just nothing but pure yellow gold all around, as if the sun had dipped its beams into the earth. Support local parks, walk, bike or jog. Or bring your fluffy best friend. Just move a bit and you'll be good! Toodles!”



Category: Parks 

Location: Energy Corridor, Houston 


Tags: Terry Hershey Park review, Energy Corridor parks, Houston hiking trails, nature walks Houston, best jogging trails Houston, scenic parks Houston

title: Voodoo Doughnut – Quirky Classics with Mixed Execution in the Washington Corridor
description: Voodoo Doughnut brings its signature pink flair and eccentric personality to Houston—but the experience doesn’t quite match the magic of its flagship locations in Portland or Austin. While the shop is undeniably fun, colorful, and great for hosting out-of-town visitors, the freshness and texture of the doughnuts can be inconsistent compared to their busier, higher-volume counterparts.Houston is full of standout donut shops, many of which offer simple, fresh, reliable classics. Voodoo leans heavi
author: Sara Loren
html:
Voodoo Doughnut brings its signature pink flair and eccentric personality to Houston—but the experience doesn’t quite match the magic of its flagship locations in Portland or Austin. While the shop is undeniably fun, colorful, and great for hosting out-of-town visitors, the freshness and texture of the doughnuts can be inconsistent compared to their busier, higher-volume counterparts.


Houston is full of standout donut shops, many of which offer simple, fresh, reliable classics. Voodoo leans heavily into novelty toppings and funky combinations—sometimes fun, sometimes too over the top. Yet in the middle of that theatrical menu, the simplest donuts end up being the unexpected stars.


What to Expect

  • Playful, quirky donut names and bright pink-themed décor

  • Less foot traffic = less frequent fresh batches

  • Best items tend to be the classic, uncomplicated donuts

  • Good hot coffee to pair with your picks


Review

Sara I. (Mar 21, 2020): 

“The doughnuts here aren’t as fresh as the Austin location. They’re not churning through batches the way they do in PDX or ATX, so things get a bit stale. The storefront lacks the charm of the original shops too. Houston has so many great donut spots—and this one just isn’t it for me.


I do enjoy the quirky pink aesthetic and their fun, funky donut names. Definitely a cute place to take visitors. But many toppings are overkill; more hype than substance. The jelly donut was the standout—full of raspberry jelly with a crisp, thick shell. The plain cake donut was another favorite: nutmeg-kissed, dense, not too sweet. The buttermilk bar was good as well. Basically, the simpler the flavor, the better it tasted.


Voodoo is supposed to be magically delicious, but things are getting stale—literally. On the bright side, the coffee is good, warm, local, and fresh. Ask for milk and pair it with your fave donut.


Overall? Probably won’t be back anytime soon.”



Category: Donuts, Desserts 

Location: Washington Corridor, Houston 


Tags: Voodoo Doughnut Houston review, quirky donut shops Texas, best classic donuts Houston, raspberry jelly donut Houston, Houston dessert spots, Portland donut import HTX

title: Bevers Kitchen & Gifts – Cozy Country Comfort in Chappell Hill
description: Bevers Kitchen & Gifts captures everything you want from a countryside eatery—warm hospitality, hearty homestyle dishes, and a dessert selection that will make any pie lover swoon. Located along a charming street lined with small, local shops, this cozy kitchen is the perfect mid-road-trip stop or weekend getaway treat.Arriving just an hour before closing still left plenty of time to enjoy a light meal and some unforgettable pie. The savory menu brings comfort in every bite, especially the stand
author: Sara Loren
html:
Bevers Kitchen & Gifts captures everything you want from a countryside eatery—warm hospitality, hearty homestyle dishes, and a dessert selection that will make any pie lover swoon. Located along a charming street lined with small, local shops, this cozy kitchen is the perfect mid-road-trip stop or weekend getaway treat.


Arriving just an hour before closing still left plenty of time to enjoy a light meal and some unforgettable pie. The savory menu brings comfort in every bite, especially the standout beef chili. Though beanless, this version delivers depth, warmth, and rich earthy spices that evoke true Texas comfort. Paired with wild rice seasoned with thyme, celery, and carrots, it makes a beautifully balanced and hearty bowl.


The beef brisket sandwich also earns praise—tender, flavorful, and exactly what you’d hope for from a small-town kitchen. But the real crown jewels here are the pies. From classic buttermilk to coconut cream with a towering meringue, each slice hits the mark with crisp crusts, balanced sweetness, and nostalgic charm.

Bevers Kitchen shines in its sweets, its simplicity, and its welcoming country vibe. A must-stop for anyone passing through Chappell Hill.


Must-Try Items:

  • Beef chili (deep, earthy, & richly spiced)

  • Wild rice side (herbaceous & comforting)

  • Beef brisket sandwich

  • Coconut cream pie with meringue

  • Buttermilk pie (classic & nostalgic)


Review

Sara I. (Mar 30, 2023): 

“What a wonderful and cozy homestyle kitchen in the countryside. I loved it here and loved everything about Bevers Kitchen & Gifts. Arrived here close to one hour before closing and had enough time to snack on some pie and a bit of savory food. Had decent leftovers because I just wanted a light bite to eat that mid-afternoon.

I loved their beef chili! I typically can't stand chili without beans, I don't want to eat beef bolognese! But theirs? Even without the beans the chili was darn good. Lots of savory and deep earthy spices. I decided to pair my chili with a side of wild rice. The wild rice was great! Earthy as well, with a tone of ground thyme and diced celery as well as carrot. Paired well with the spicy beef chili. Yum.


I liked their beef brisket sandwich as well, which I got to try a bite from my partner. The service was friendly and chill, so was the environment. It's also nestled within a cozy street full of little shops that are unique to the area.


Having a sweet tooth, I was impressed with the pies at Bevers kitchen. Hadn't had buttermilk pie in eons. Coconut cream pie with meringue.. good stuff. I was afraid the meringue would be sickly sweet. Nope. The meringue was piled high and cut well with the creaminess of the coconut cream. The pie crust? Absolute crisp. They shine with their sweets and I'll definitely revisit to try another pie when in the area. This spot is recommended by Sara the pastry gal. Go!”



Category: American, New American 

Location: Chappell Hill, Texas


 Tags: Bevers Kitchen review, Chappell Hill restaurants, Texas country cooking, best pies Texas, buttermilk pie review, homestyle dining Texas, comfort food road trip

title: Thai Orchid – Fiery Flavors with Laotian & Cambodian Influence
description: Thai Orchid brings bold heat, vibrant flavors, and a menu that stretches beyond traditional Thai fare into memorable Laotian and Cambodian dishes. This unassuming spot in North Houston/Spring delivers intensity—especially for diners who think they can handle any level of spice. The food is fresh, flavorful, and unapologetically fiery, balanced by warm service and a family-owned atmosphere.What to Expect • A massive menu with Thai staples plus standout Laotian/Cambodian dishes. • Serious spice le
author: Sara Loren
html:
Thai Orchid brings bold heat, vibrant flavors, and a menu that stretches beyond traditional Thai fare into memorable Laotian and Cambodian dishes. This unassuming spot in North Houston/Spring delivers intensity—especially for diners who think they can handle any level of spice. The food is fresh, flavorful, and unapologetically fiery, balanced by warm service and a family-owned atmosphere.


What to Expect

  • A massive menu with Thai staples plus standout Laotian/Cambodian dishes.

  • Serious spice levels—even seasoned heat lovers will be challenged.

  • Fresh ingredients and deep, complex flavors across salads, soups, and noodles.

  • Simple decor, friendly owners, and a casual local-diner feel.


Must-Try Items

  • Som Tum (Papaya Salad) – intensely spicy, crisp, sour, and addictive

  • Tom Yum Soup – bright, aromatic, and customizable to vegetarian

  • Laad Nah – silky dark gravy over noodles with broccoli, onions, and your choice of protein

  • Iced Thai Coffee – sweet, cold, and the perfect antidote to the heat


Review

Sara I. (Nov 15, 2021): 

“This restaurant really brought in the heat. I thought I could handle any spice level until I met Thai Orchid on a random Sunday night. The best items on the menu are definitely the Laotian and Cambodian-influenced dishes. The Som Tum is the total winner—super crisp, sour, and spicy. I honestly couldn’t handle the heat at first, but after a moment to catch my breath, I inhaled most of it. The Thai iced coffee was the saving grace.


The Tom Yum had plenty of depth and zest, packed with fresh tomatoes, shrimp, and mushrooms, and can be made vegetarian. I loved their Laad Nah—dark gravy, broccoli, onions, and chicken, savory and slightly sweet, and a great balance to the spicy dishes.


The menu is huge, the food is fresh, and the owners are friendly. Decor is simple, but the flavors shine. If you’re in North Houston or passing through Spring, I recommend stopping by. Support local biz!”


Category: Thai, Cambodian 

Location: Houston, TX 


Tags: Thai Orchid Houston review, spicy Thai food Houston, Laotian cuisine Houston, Cambodian restaurants Texas, Som Tum Houston, Tom Yum Spring TX

title: Dolce & Cafe – A Quaint Spring Branch Spot with Room to Grow
description: Dolce & Cafe brings a whimsical, European-inspired charm to Spring Branch with its cozy interior, spacious seating, and an extensive menu of crepes, brunch favorites, and pastries. The atmosphere leans warm and quaint, though the dark interior creates a moody ambiance that contrasts with the sweetness suggested by its name. While the café stays busy with guests enjoying savory items and brunch plates, service and consistency can vary depending on the day.Though the experience may not shine on ev
author: Sara Loren
html:
Dolce & Cafe brings a whimsical, European-inspired charm to Spring Branch with its cozy interior, spacious seating, and an extensive menu of crepes, brunch favorites, and pastries. The atmosphere leans warm and quaint, though the dark interior creates a moody ambiance that contrasts with the sweetness suggested by its name. While the café stays busy with guests enjoying savory items and brunch plates, service and consistency can vary depending on the day.


Though the experience may not shine on every visit, the menu offers promise—from flaky pastries to made-to-order crepes—and this neighborhood spot still holds potential for a sweeter return.


Must-Try Items (to explore on a future visit):

  • Sweet & Savory Crepes

  • French Toast

  • Warm Pastries

  • Hot Coffee Options


Reviews

Sara I. (May 2, 2022):

“Oh gosh, such stiff and awkward service upon stepping into this local cafe. This cafe is quaint and whimsical inside. The interior is quite dark though. The seats are plentiful and decently comfortable. The service? Not so much. The young lady just stared at us bleakly as we stared at her right back. No hi, hello, or anything. Not even a smile.


I uncomfortably ordered an iced coffee. I then paused and asked if she could add 2% milk to it. Then she finally, yet bleakly responded. Hallelujah, I guess. My friend ordered an iced tea, along with a pastry. Our orders came quietly onto our table, followed by the pastry that was getting toasted a bit in their oven.


The iced coffee was by far the worst tasting coffee I have ever had. It had zero flavor, aroma or anything that could even remind you of coffee. It was completely flat and bitter tasting. Nothing. It was a warm day out—but I'm thinking their warm coffee is better tasting, given their reviews. The pastry was warm and crisp, flaky and lightly sweet.


I may revisit & try a crepe or their French toast. But I'm having mixed feelings. The city of Houston has plenty of memorable cafes to offer. This might have just been an off day. Other than that, the cafe was busy with folk enjoying their crepes and savory items. The menu is quite extensive. Dolce means sweet in Italian; and our experience was quite the contrary. May bump up the review if a more pleasant experience is encountered on a prospective visit.”



Category: Creperies, Breakfast & Brunch, Sandwiches 

Location: Spring Branch, Houston 


Tags: Dolce & Cafe Houston review, Spring Branch brunch, Houston creperies, local cafés Houston, iced coffee Houston, brunch spots near Spring Branch

author: Sara Loren
html:
Tucked beneath a canopy of trees along Grogan’s Drive, Third Gen Coffee feels like a cozy escape—a quiet, woodsy nook with nostalgic winter charm and the warmth of a true neighborhood café. From the moment you step inside, its character shines through: soft lighting, inviting décor, and the unexpected charm of a staircase that leads to a peaceful second-floor lounge.


Upstairs, guests find couches, tables, and charging outlets, making it an ideal setting for studying, reading, or lingering with a warm drink. Seasonal beverages bring extra joy, and the standout this visit was a hot eggnog latte—creamy, festive, and deliciously comforting.


Friendly service and thoughtfully crafted drinks round out the experience, making Third Gen Coffee a must-visit for those seeking a serene moment in The Woodlands. Whether you’re passing through or planning a cozy café day, this corner shop offers warmth, charm, and the kind of atmosphere that invites you to return again and again.


What to Try:

  • Hot eggnog latte (seasonal favorite)

  • Seasonal specialty drinks

  • Classic espresso beverages


Atmosphere Highlights:

  • Woodsy surroundings with crisp air

  • Upstairs seating with outlets

  • Cozy, warm, and inviting aesthetic

  • Friendly, attentive baristas


Review

Sara I. (Jan 2, 2023): 

“Such a great little coffee shoppe tucked in the Woodlands on Grograns drive. I'm diggin' this quiet little corner, cluttered with trees and a few stores lined up together. The air felt & smelled crisp and it totally was nostalgic of some sort of northern winter. Wanting to visit the local bookshop next time.


What I liked most about this coffee shoppe? It's charm and characteristic. That's the first thing I noticed upon stepping in. A bit of light and warmth all around, and a staircase that leads you to the second floor. Ample seating upstairs with a few tables, couch and charging outlets.


They have a few unique flavoured drinks this time of the year. My favorite being the eggnog latte.. but make it hot. I look forward to revisiting and trying different items off the menu, in particular, their seasonal products.

It was a great local experience at third gen coffee, the staff was friendly and the drinks were crafted with love. I totally look forward to revisiting if ever in the area.”

Location: The Woodlands, Texas

Known for both dairy and vegan flavors, this spot instantly fits into Houston’s dessert landscape—elevated, indulgent, and full of personality.During its grand opening, the shop buzzed with friendly service, fresh waffle cones, and a lineup of flavors that ranged from classic comfort to floral, elegant creations. Whether you’re grabbi
author: Sara Loren
html:
Van Leeuwen brings its New York–born charm straight into the heart of Montrose, offering ultra-creamy, thoughtfully crafted ice creams in a cozy, polished setting. Known for both dairy and vegan flavors, this spot instantly fits into Houston’s dessert landscape—elevated, indulgent, and full of personality.


During its grand opening, the shop buzzed with friendly service, fresh waffle cones, and a lineup of flavors that ranged from classic comfort to floral, elegant creations. Whether you’re grabbing a cone before wandering the Montrose Collective plaza or cooling down after a warm Houston afternoon, this shop promises a scoop worth savoring.


Must-Try Items:

  • Royal Wedding Cake Ice Cream – sweet cream cheese base, lemon sponge cake chunks, elderflower frosting

  • Honeycomb Ice Cream – a house classic, perfectly paired with a crisp waffle cone

  • Fresh Waffle Cones – hot, fragrant, and delightfully crunchy

  • Vegan Flavors – signature offerings for dairy-free dessert lovers


Reviews

Sara I. (Apr 28, 2022): “Creamy and dreamy, refreshing ice-cream.

I visited exactly a month ago with a good friend of mine. I had never tried Van Leeuwen although I spotted it a few times out in New York. That's where VL is originally from and it's great to have a spot here down in the H. This is not their first location but it's definitely a cozy spot to open up shoppe.


We have plenty of ice-cream spots in the area but us gourmand Houstonians will happily welcome any new kid on the block. All prestigious and cute, we visited during their grand opening. Truly was a great experience, folks were friendly and fast, whipping up batches and scooping ’em up in cones or cups. I was sooo excited to try their Royal Wedding cake flavor and it was darn good!


Royal Wedding Cake ice cream: ‘Floral, sweet cream cheese ice cream. Chunks of lemon sponge cake layered with elderflower frosting.’


Another flavor that's a total classic is their honeycomb ice cream. It paired perfectly with their crispy and fresh waffle cone.


I was delighted. The flavor I got was regal, classy and sweet. I'm a fan of elderflower notes and the lemon definitely spritzied up the flavor. This spot has always been known for their vegan flavors, but dairy lovers can rejoice—they’ve got plenty of classic options too.


I thought VL would outdo itself in a not-good way, but it was great and I'm happy to welcome this spot to the new Montrose Collective plaza. Toodle-oo! You'll be a sweet spot to savor during these warmer months ahead. Keep calm, chill out, and eat some ice cream!”



Category: Ice Cream & Frozen Yogurt, Desserts, Sandwiches 

Location: Montrose, Houston 


Tags: Van Leeuwen Montrose, Houston ice cream shops, Royal Wedding Cake ice cream, honeycomb ice cream Houston, Montrose Collective desserts, artisanal ice cream TX

Matcha nama chocolate stole
author: Sara Loren
html:
The ROYCE’ Chocolate tasting event in Chinatown offered a creamy, dreamy escape into the world of premium Japanese confections. Known for its ultra-smooth textures and high-quality ingredients sourced from northern Japan, ROYCE’ brings the spirit of Hokkaido’s celebrated dairy culture straight into Houston — and this event showcased the very best of it.


Guests enjoyed samples of the brand’s famous nama chocolates, each piece velvety, rich, and melt-in-your-mouth soft. Matcha nama chocolate stole the spotlight—earthy, bittersweet, and beautifully balanced with the creaminess that ROYCE’ is known for. Pistachio-studded varieties and other flavor infusions added to the international flair and indulgence.


Service throughout the event was warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, making it easy to learn about the origins, ingredients, and craftsmanship behind each chocolate. Though the visit was brief, it was packed with flavor, quality, and appreciation for Japanese confectionery artistry.


Event Highlights:

  • Samples of ROYCE’s iconic nama chocolates

  • Matcha nama chocolate: a must-try, tea-forward delight

  • Unique flavor variations like pistachio

  • Insight into Hokkaido dairy culture and confectionery origins

  • Friendly, prompt customer service

  • A fun, flavorful stop within Chinatown’s bustling food scene


Review

Sara I. (Jun 1, 2023):

“Such creamy, dreamy and ultra decadent chocolates at ROYCE chocolatiers! This spot is awesome and has such an international vibe because of the ingredients they showcase within their chocolates. Pistachios and so many other variations within their chocolate! I love it and purchased the pistachio variation.


ROYCE originates from northern Japan... from an area known for its dairy products. I have always loved products originating from Hokkaido, such as their milk breads and cheese tarts + many other items. These chocolates are of no other exception... so milky and creamy with every bite you take... especially their famous ‘nama’ chocolates which were provided as samples for this event. My favorite being their matcha nama chocolate sample. Soo good. Love anything with matcha! You could taste the quality of the fine tea leaves meshed with the creaminess of the cacao beans.


Service was good, prompt and attentive. Just stayed for a bit as I was headed to an appointment somewhere else. Everything was appreciated though in regards to chocolate samples and answering all of my questions.

Cheers and SYOY.”



Category: Specialty Food Events, Chocolate & Confectionery 

Location: Chinatown, Houston 


Tags: ROYCE chocolate Houston, Japanese chocolate tasting, nama chocolate event, Hokkaido desserts, Chinatown specialty shops, premium chocolate Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
Whit N Wingo is the kind of vintage shop that immediately pulls you in with its color, charm, and treasure-hunt energy. Nestled in EaDo along Harrisburg, this vibrant boutique is packed wall-to-wall with personality—rings, tote bags, clothing, knick-knacks, playful trinkets, and an ever-changing mix of curiosities. It’s a space made for wandering, exploring, and discovering something unexpected.


One of the standout features? They stay open late—a rare treat in the world of vintage retail. Whether you're grabbing ice cream, finishing up pizza in the plaza, or simply looking for a fun nighttime stroll, Whit N Wingo offers a warm, whimsical place to browse. Friendly service (shoutout to Zach!), welcoming vibes, and a rainbow of items make it an unforgettable stop for fashion lovers and curious shoppers alike.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Late-night browsing for night owls and explorers

  • A colorful selection of vintage jewelry, clothing, and quirky finds

  • Friendly, knowledgeable staff

  • Located next to other fun shops, perfect for post-dinner exploring

  • Kid-friendly trinkets and tote bags for gifting


Reviews

Sara I. (Jun 8, 2025 – First to Review):

 “Quite a unique vintage shoppe, very colorful with so many items on display and for purchase. I found a few cute rings here and I just love wearing them. I met with Zach and he was friendly and knowledgeable about the shoppe. He explained to me that they stay opened late, so this is definitely a spot you can hang out late at night and just browse around. They have plenty of knick-knacks and cool stuff overall. Whit N Wingo is right by a few other fun stores, so definitely drop by here after getting some ice cream or pizza in the same plaza. They had some nice tote bags here a few little toys that I would get for my son next time. Overall, a very colorful shoppe to stop by when in the Harrisburg (Eado) area.”

title: Tacos Doña Lena – Homestyle Mexican Comfort in Spring Branch
description: Tacos Doña Lena is one of those unassuming neighborhood gems where the food speaks louder than the décor. This tiny, bustling taquería brings big, bright flavors to the table—fresh salsas, warm tortillas, and lovingly prepared plates that echo the warmth of a family kitchen. With constant to-go orders flying out and tables filled at all hours, it’s clear this place has earned its loyal following.Expect a welcoming staff, a spotless dining area, and an impressive selection of sauces and fresh dri
author: Sara Loren
html:
Tacos Doña Lena is one of those unassuming neighborhood gems where the food speaks louder than the décor. This tiny, bustling taquería brings big, bright flavors to the table—fresh salsas, warm tortillas, and lovingly prepared plates that echo the warmth of a family kitchen. With constant to-go orders flying out and tables filled at all hours, it’s clear this place has earned its loyal following.


Expect a welcoming staff, a spotless dining area, and an impressive selection of sauces and fresh drinks that elevate every bite. Whether you’re craving tacos, tostadas, quesadillas, or something more adventurous, this spot truly embodies the comforting heart of Mexican street food.


Must-Try Items

  • Grande Avocado Quesadilla – warm, cheesy, generously filled, deeply satisfying

  • Crispy Tostada – crunchy, flavorful, great with any of the fresh salsas

  • Tacos (any variety) – vibrant, authentic flavors reminiscent of Yucatán cooking

  • Aguas Frescas – house-made with real fruit chunks and natural sweetness

  • Vegetarian Options – beans and tortillas made without lard; try the nopal or soups


Review

Sara I. (Apr 28, 2021):

“Absolutely amazing tacos in this hole-in-the-wall joint. Zesty food made by zesty and kind folk. Some of their food took me back to the Yucatán peninsula. The comida takes time to get to the table, but it’s worth it. Tons of to-go orders and tables scattered around the spot, yet the staff are big on courtesy and cleanliness.


There are about six fresh, in-house-made salsas to enjoy, and the aguas frescas are made with real fruit and pulp—sweet, cold, and perfect with savory food. I truly recommend the grande avocado quesadilla and the crispy tostada. Heck, the tacos are great too.


The menu is flexible and accommodating for any palate. Plenty of vegetarian items, and the beans and tortillas are vegetarian (no lard). Bonus points! Looking forward to revisiting and trying the nopal and soup. Glad to have a warm spot like Doña Lena in the neighborhood.”


Category: Tacos 

Location: Spring Branch, Houston 


Tags: Spring Branch tacos, Houston hole-in-the-wall eats, Yucatán-inspired flavors Houston, aguas frescas Houston, vegetarian-friendly Mexican food, handmade tortillas Houston
