author: Sara Loren
html:
Foam Coffee House brings a fun and unexpected pairing to Gulfton: a neighborhood café built right beside a car wash. While your car gets a shine, you can settle inside for a warm drink surrounded by marble textures, teal accents, and local artwork. The pastry selection is limited, but the coffee menu is straightforward and crafted with care—making it a casual, low-key stop for cappuccino lovers and locals passing through.


What to Order

  • Cappuccino – Frothy top, smooth body, and nicely balanced flavor. 

  • Morningstar Vegan Donut – A local treat when available. 

  • Hot Latte – A safe, simple choice from their classic menu.


Review

Sara I. (Feb 28, 2019):

“Liking the concept of Foam Coffee House… your vehicle can get a good scrub-a-dub-dub while you sip on a frothy beverage. A car wash is present within the small lot. I haven't used their car wash service as this review is solely based on the cafe.


Upon entering, you'll notice a few works of art, marbled walls, and a brightly colored teal wall. Pastries are far and few… mostly sad looking. They do carry a few Morningstar donuts, which happen to be local and vegan.

The menu is classic and simple—coffee and tea beverages. I opted for a cappuccino, my default these days. A good cappuccino must have a nice frothy top yet enough substantial liquid to call it a beverage. It was nicely prepared and had a good flavor to it. Warm and smooth.


Will I be back to try a few other drinks? Most definitely. But… just one word of advice: please get rid of that strange smell that permeates deep within the cafe. When I enter a coffee house, I'd like for it to be surrounded by the warm scent of coffee beans. Even the smell of a car wash would do at this point. But you get the message…”



Category: Coffee & Tea, Bakeries 

Location: Gulfton, Houston, TX 


Tags: Houston coffee shops, Gulfton cafés, cappuccino Houston, local vegan pastries Houston, unique cafés Houston

title: Gyro Republic – NYC-Style Halal Plates with a Texas Twist
description: Gyro Republic brings the classic New York–style chicken-and-rice experience to the heart of Sugar Land. Tucked inside a large shopping center, it’s an easy spot to miss unless someone points it out—yet it delivers bold flavor, generous veggie portions, and friendly service from the crew behind the counter. The platters come loaded with crisp chopped salad, creamy sauces, and your choice of chicken, gyro meat, or both. Their yellow rice is a standout: fragrant with turmeric and cardamom, warm, an
author: Sara Loren
html:
Gyro Republic brings the classic New York–style chicken-and-rice experience to the heart of Sugar Land. Tucked inside a large shopping center, it’s an easy spot to miss unless someone points it out—yet it delivers bold flavor, generous veggie portions, and friendly service from the crew behind the counter. The platters come loaded with crisp chopped salad, creamy sauces, and your choice of chicken, gyro meat, or both. Their yellow rice is a standout: fragrant with turmeric and cardamom, warm, and satisfying enough to savor on its own. While the flavor foundation is strong, much of the menu leans heavily salty, especially when combined with sauces, jalapeños, and pickles—something to keep in mind when customizing your order.


Review

Sara I. (Jan 5, 2020):

“I’ve visited twice recently, and Gyro Republic is a spot I would’ve overlooked if not for my cousin’s recommendation. They serve up classic platters and wraps—halal, hearty, and full of crunch from freshly chopped vegetables. The chicken has an orange tint, likely from a tikka-style marinade, and the gyro meat is crisp and tender, though both are quite salty. Pairing everything with their sauces and pickles makes it even saltier, which is too bad because the overall flavors are good.


Their yellow rice is my favorite—aromatic with turmeric and cardamom. I could honestly eat a bowl of it on its own. The guys behind the counter are friendly, and overall service has been solid. It’s nice having a NY-style chicken-and-rice spot in town, complete with fresh fruit and vegetable juices to round out the menu. I may swing by again, but the recipes could use a little refinement. Until next time!”


Category: Halal, Fast Food, Mediterranean 

Location: Sugar Land, TX

title: Bouchée Patisserie – Whimsical Sweets & Parisian Charm in Uptown
description: A dreamy, candy-land-meets-Paris patisserie nestled inside the Post Oak Hotel, Bouchée Patisserie is a visual and culinary escape. Warm lights, elegant décor, and soft Parisian music create an atmosphere that feels transported straight from France—perfect for brunch dates, out-of-town guests, or an indulgent post-Galleria treat. From flaky croissants to citrus-kissed madeleines, this pâtisserie balances whimsy with refined craftsmanship.What to Order • Almond Croissant – Ultra buttery, crispy, w
author: Sara Loren
html:
A dreamy, candy-land-meets-Paris patisserie nestled inside the Post Oak Hotel, Bouchée Patisserie is a visual and culinary escape. Warm lights, elegant décor, and soft Parisian music create an atmosphere that feels transported straight from France—perfect for brunch dates, out-of-town guests, or an indulgent post-Galleria treat. From flaky croissants to citrus-kissed madeleines, this pâtisserie balances whimsy with refined craftsmanship.


What to Order

  • Almond Croissant – Ultra buttery, crispy, warm, deeply satisfying.

  • Madeleine – Spongy, citrusy, classic, and perfect for dunking.

  • Hot Chocolate – Foamy, cozy, and a gentle pairing for pastries.


Review

Sara I. (Apr 9, 2019):

“Dream land… candy land… a whimsical pastry boutique of sorts. Walk in at anytime and you'll be fascinated upon the selection of tempting treats. Bouchee Patisserie is a lovely cafe to bring family, friends and out of town guests. Or maybe even a boujie date night? If that's your thing.


I recommend visiting on the weekend after having brunch in the city & dropping by for sweets. Bouchee is tucked within the inner loop and nearby to the Houston Galleria—perfect area to take a stroll or check out the Post Oak Hotel which is connected to the cafe. Even visiting at night is such a delight with all the vivid colors glowing inside the pâtisserie.


The Parisian music transported my dining partner and I to France. Totally felt like we were elsewhere—in a good way. With so many items to choose from, we decided on the madeleine and almond croissant. Paired our pastries with a plain black coffee and hot chocolate. We found the drinks to be plain in taste—the hot chocolate was foamy, but not tall, dark, and handsome like my date. Guess he made up for it?


The hedonistic treats took center stage: the croissant was super buttery and crispy, and the madeleine spongy and citrusy. I can easily judge a cafe by its simple baked items… and this madeleine was one of the best I've had. Dunked into a warm beverage, such a delight. (One might remember Marcel Proust’s memoir In Search of Lost Time—storytime, y’all.)


Anyway… what are you waiting for? Grab any of the croissants—plain or almond—and make sure they heat it up for ya. Crunch factor sound on and relish in delight! Save me a little crumb in which I may encounter the warm memoir of Marcel Proust… Ciao.”



Category: Patisserie, Cake Shop, Cafés 

Location: Galleria / Uptown, Houston, TX

title: Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ – Express Eats Inside HMart Katy
description: Tucked inside the bustling HMart food court, this express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ offers a slimmed-down menu compared to the full-service locations in Bellaire and Sugar Land. While the convenience is great for a quick meal during grocery runs, the service and execution can vary, and some signature elements—like sizzling hot tofu soup and a full spread of banchan—may feel pared back.Still, certain dishes shine, such as their surprisingly crisp seafood pancake. For diners who already know
author: Sara Loren
html:
Tucked inside the bustling HMart food court, this express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ offers a slimmed-down menu compared to the full-service locations in Bellaire and Sugar Land. While the convenience is great for a quick meal during grocery runs, the service and execution can vary, and some signature elements—like sizzling hot tofu soup and a full spread of banchan—may feel pared back.


Still, certain dishes shine, such as their surprisingly crisp seafood pancake. For diners who already know and love the brand, this location delivers familiar flavors in a more fast-casual format, though it may not fully match the consistency and breadth of the standalone restaurants.


Review

Sara I. (Jan 21, 2020):

“This seems to be an express version of Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ, tucked inside the newer HMart in Katy. Having visited the Bellaire and Sugar Land locations, I’ve always liked their food and menu options.


Service here, however, was dull and lackluster. I ordered tofu soup with mushrooms and asked for kimchi in my soup. When it arrived, it wasn’t bubbling as it normally does in cast-iron bowls. No kimchi in sight, and the flavor lacked the usual sharp, spicy kick. I also noticed there was no egg—normally you crack a raw egg into the hot soup for that creamy binding factor. Without it, the soup felt watery and flat. My friend asked for an egg, but the cashier said they didn’t offer that. Oddly enough, when I went up later, I saw a sign stating you can request an egg. Strange.


Banchan was limited to three small items. The other locations typically offer six. I guess that’s the express trade-off.


The seafood pancake, though, was crisp and well-balanced—probably the best item we had. Not doughy or soggy, and the crunch held up even after a while.


Overall, the meal was just okay. Healthy at least? Many of the other cafeteriastyle stalls serve fried or greasy food, which isn’t my vibe. I’ll likely stick to this HMart for grocery shopping rather than meals.”


Category: Korean 

Location: Katy, TX 


Tags: Korean tofu soup Katy, HMart Katy food court, Korean comfort food Houston suburbs, soondubu Katy, Korean seafood pancake Houston

With whimsical animal art, a relaxed aesthetic, and plenty of seating, it’s a breezy place to work, socialize, or unwind before a stroll through the park. author: Sara Loren
html:
Slowpokes’ Upper Kirby outpost brings the brand’s signature laid-back charm right across from Levy Park. With whimsical animal art, a relaxed aesthetic, and plenty of seating, it’s a breezy place to work, socialize, or unwind before a stroll through the park. Three hours of validated garage parking makes it even more appealing for inner-loopers looking to avoid the usual parking chaos.


The café offers a wide range of drinks—coffee, wine, tea, and house snacks—and while the beans run on the stronger, sharper side, the environment makes lingering here easy. Service is friendly, seating is ample, and both indoor and outdoor options keep the space lively but never overwhelming.


What to Order

  • Latte (try the rose syrup version)

  • Cappuccino

  • House Snacks or Small Plates


Review

Sara I. (Mar 22, 2019): 

“Digging this second location of Slowpokes and liking how it's nestled within the inner loop. The location is stellar—right across Levy park with plenty of parking situated within the garage. You get in a good three hours of free parking within the garage, as long as you get your ticket validated upon leaving the cafe. There's also a bit of outside parking as well within a three hour timeframe.


Upon entering, you'll notice a few whimsical paintings of sloths, snails and turtles. All things cute and slow. Liking the unique concept as well as the decor. Slowpokes has quite a few items in terms of their beverage menu. Plenty of snacks and foodish items as well.


I opted for a latte and asked which sort of syrups they had. The barista recommended a rose latte and that caught my attention rather quickly. Being a fan of rose flavored anything, I went ahead and ordered the latte that she suggested. Service was friendly and the latte was brought promptly to my table. Although I enjoyed my latte, I really couldn't taste any of the rose flavor. The coffee beans are sour and strong here— not the smooth finish type. Latte was generously filled to the brim and I couldn't finish it all.


Next time I'll opt for a cappuccino. Overall I'm diggin' the vibes, music and aesthetic appeal. Nothing hipster, cramped or stuffy about Slowpokes. It's great to have yet another coffee house within Houston—one that I'll definitely frequent.”



Category: Coffee & Tea, Wine Bars

Location: Upper Kirby, Houston 


Tags: Slowpokes Houston, Levy Park coffee, Houston café reviews, rose latte Houston, best coffee shops inner loop

title: Asia Blue – Modern Taiwanese Fusion with Room to Grow
description: Asia Blue brings a fresh, modern presence to Tang City Plaza, pairing sleek décor with an open kitchen and a digital menu that makes browsing fun and easy. The atmosphere is polished, bright, and inviting, with warm service and attention to presentation. While the appetizers and tea shine, the entrées—particularly the vegetarian curry noodle soup and laksa—leave room for improvement. Even so, the freshness of the ingredients and the lack of MSG make it worth revisiting, especially as the restaur
author: Sara Loren
html:
Asia Blue brings a fresh, modern presence to Tang City Plaza, pairing sleek décor with an open kitchen and a digital menu that makes browsing fun and easy. The atmosphere is polished, bright, and inviting, with warm service and attention to presentation. While the appetizers and tea shine, the entrées—particularly the vegetarian curry noodle soup and laksa—leave room for improvement. Even so, the freshness of the ingredients and the lack of MSG make it worth revisiting, especially as the restaurant continues to establish its footing in this growing food hub.


Review

Sara I. (Dec 21, 2019): 

“I wanted to really love this new spot! The vibe is charming—modern interior, clean and sparkly décor, and an open kitchen where you can watch the chefs at work. The tablet-style menu is a neat touch, making it easy to swipe through photos and descriptions.


We started with vegetarian spring rolls that arrived piping hot and super crisp—definitely made in-house. Paired them with herbal tea served in adorable teapots, which I highly recommend ordering while you wait for your meal.


For mains, I chose the vegetarian curry noodle soup and my friend ordered the laksa. Both dishes were beautifully presented, mine garnished with alfalfa sprouts and plenty of veggies, but the flavors fell flat. The toasted sesame oil seemed to overshadow the curry notes, and I missed the brightness of citrus and spice. My friend felt similarly about the laksa. I added salt and chili to bump it up a bit, and the leftovers actually tasted better the next day.


Still, I appreciated the freshness and the fact that nothing had MSG. Sometimes simple, real ingredients speak louder than anything else. I’m curious to try their Taiwanese-style beef noodle soup next—likely one of their stronger offerings.


Tang City Plaza is the new, up-and-coming hotspot for Sugar Land and Missouri City, so I’ll definitely be back. Noodle soup in this weather is always comforting, and I’m hopeful for an improved experience. Until next time!”



Category: Asian Fusion, Ramen, Taiwanese 

Location: Missouri City, TX

title: Bismillah Restaurant & Café – Halal Comfort, Big Portions & a Fresh New Look in Sharpstown
description: Bismillah Restaurant & Café has transformed its space with a brighter, cleaner, and more expansive layout—perfect for families, groups, and anyone craving halal comfort food with a South Asian twist. A colorful Houston-themed mural and glowing lighting fixtures give the restaurant a playful-yet-ethereal feel, while the menu blends American classics with Pakistani street-food favorites.What to Order • Classic Burger – Fresh, melty, satisfying, and far more balanced than the spicier options.  • Pa
author: Sara Loren
html:
Bismillah Restaurant & Café has transformed its space with a brighter, cleaner, and more expansive layout—perfect for families, groups, and anyone craving halal comfort food with a South Asian twist. A colorful Houston-themed mural and glowing lighting fixtures give the restaurant a playful-yet-ethereal feel, while the menu blends American classics with Pakistani street-food favorites.


What to Order

  • Classic Burger – Fresh, melty, satisfying, and far more balanced than the spicier options. 

  • Papdi Chaat – Crisp, sweet-savory, and a crowd-pleasing South Asian classic. 

  • Cajun Fries – Salty, bold, and generously portioned.


Review

Sara I. (Jan 20, 2019):

“I had dinner at Bismillah Café with my mother last night. I specifically came because I heard about the recent renovations—and I hadn’t been in ages. The restaurant is now in a bigger space with a cleaner, brighter look. Plenty of seating for large families and gatherings. There’s even a large painted mural depicting Houston icons—playful and unique. The lighting gives the whole place an ethereal feel.


I don’t normally eat burgers, but I was craving one. I decided on the Diablo burger because it sounded intriguing. I'm a fan of spicy food and figured I could handle it. The lady at the register, who was friendly, recommended it as well. My mom ordered the papdi chaat—an item recently suggested to me, and my mom loves chaat anyway. Both of our orders came out around the same time, and everything tasted fresh.


Unfortunately, the Diablo burger was too spicy for me. The hot sauce had a grainy texture and tasted a bit raw. The burger had all the works—lettuce, onion, tomato—but the cucumbers threw me off. I guess they were added for fusion flair. The Cajun fries that came with it were a heaping pile—salty and overwhelming on top of an already intense burger. I ended up ordering the classic burger because I simply couldn’t eat the first one.


The manager was friendly and brought out the new burger, which was far better. He chatted with us and asked how everything was—something I appreciated, as it made the experience feel homier. The classic burger came with all the basics, minus cucumbers. Melty cheese, ketchup, big bun, big patty—all fresh. I only ate half, but I enjoyed it.


The papdi chaat was crisp and well-balanced, with garbanzo beans and potatoes blanketed in a sweet and savory sauce. Overall, the service was warm, the food fresh, and the dining experience pleasant. I can definitely see myself coming back with family to try other items. I’m not normally in the area, but I recommend everyone visit the newly renovated Bismillah Café. They have something for everyone.”



Category: Burgers, Halal, Pakistani

Location: Sharpstown, Houston, TX 


Tags: Halal burgers Houston, Pakistani chaat Houston, Sharpstown restaurants, fusion burgers Houston, family-friendly halal spots

title: The Original Marini’s Empanada House – Classic Argentine Comfort in Westchase
description: A long-loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old-world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada. The interior glows with nostalgic character, and the atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming—plus, the owners’ friendly cats occasionally roam outside, adding even more personality to this neighborhood gem. With an extensive menu spanning savory classics, creative fillings, and sweet dessert blends, there’s truly an empanada for everyone.What
author: Sara Loren
html:
A long-loved Houston institution, The Original Marini’s Empanada House delivers warmth, charm, and old-world comfort with every crispy, freshly fried empanada. The interior glows with nostalgic character, and the atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming—plus, the owners’ friendly cats occasionally roam outside, adding even more personality to this neighborhood gem. With an extensive menu spanning savory classics, creative fillings, and sweet dessert blends, there’s truly an empanada for everyone.


What to Order

  • Beef Picadillo (Beef Gaucho) – Juicy, classic, and the perfect pairing with green chili sauce. 

  • Chicken Poblana (Mole) – Earthy, deep chocolate notes, rich and comforting. 

  • Dessert Empanada: Elvis Melbis – Peanut butter + banana + dulce de leche indulgence.


Reviews

Sara I. (Jan 20, 2019):

“They have cats upon the premises! That's the main reason I dined in here a couple of days ago. Jk. I had dinner here a few nights ago with a good friend. Both of the cats belong to the owners and normally just patrol outside—not inside.


This was my first time at Marini's, though my friend Mike had been here before. The interior is warm and glowing, with plenty of seating. There’s a historical appeal inside Marini’s, and I'm surprised it took me so long to visit.


On a crisp and chilly night, empanadas were just the right items to nosh on. The menu is large and thoroughly categorized—there’s truly an empanada for everyone. I ordered two savory empanadas and one dessert: the chicken poblana (mole), the beef picadillo (beef gaucho), and the Elvis melbis for dessert (peanut butter, banana, dulce de leche).


Everything is made fresh to order, and the taste reflects the quality. Service was prompt and attentive. All three empanadas were delicious—warm, crispy, freshly fried. I couldn’t finish them all and took a few bites to-go. The chicken mole was deep, earthy, and had a unique savory chocolate flavor. My favorite was the beef picadillo—juicy and perfect with the green chili sauce. When it comes to empanadas, I prefer fried over baked, and these were executed beautifully.


The dessert empanada was rich and sweet—the dulce de leche paired nicely with the banana and peanut butter, though I’ll try another flavor next time. With so many options, I look forward to exploring more of the menu. Marini’s also serves soups, salads, and more. Since it carries an Argentinian flair, you’ll find iced yerba mate by the counter. It was watered down in flavor, but still refreshing.


Chill atmosphere and warm food for the soul. Try the Original Marini’s for yourself—it's a Houston classic.

PS – I might just revisit to hang out with the cats.”



Category: Latin American, Argentine, Empanadas

Location: Westchase, Houston, TX

author: Sara Loren
html:
Amorino brings a touch of European indulgence to Highland Village, offering artisanal gelato and sorbet crafted with premium ingredients—many imported from around the world. The shop is warm, polished, and often buzzing with people, especially on festive evenings when the surrounding plaza glows with lights and activity. Known for their signature gelato “flower” cones, vibrant sorbets, rich chocolate flavors, and elegant pastries, Amorino is a favorite local stop for anyone craving a refined dessert experience.


What to Order

  • Three-Flavor Sorbet Cup – Passionfruit, Black Currant & Raspberry (bright, tart, and intensely fruity). 

  • Chocolate Gelato – Deep, decadent, and perfect for dairy lovers. 

  • Macarons Filled with Gelato – Petite, elegant, and ideal for a sweet add-on.


Review

Sara I. (Dec 31, 2018):

“Ahh! I'm a big fan of sorbet… and this place totally satisfied my craving for all things sorbet related. Amorino serves authentic gelato, waffles, chocolates, coffee beverages, and even pound cakes and macarons. The shop was packed the night I visited—Christmas night—and luckily Amorino was open in this lively part of town. The River Oaks District plaza was glowing with lights and people wandering around.


Amorino has quite a selection of sorbets and gelato, with many of the fruit elements imported from various countries. I chose the smallest cup, which fits three flavors. Without hesitation, I picked the passionfruit, black currant, and raspberry—side by side. I’m so glad I chose them. They were crisp, tart, and full of fresh fruit flavor. Honestly, some of the best sorbet I've ever had!


I definitely want to revisit this cute little shoppe to try their dairy-based gelato—several chocolate flavors caught my eye. Now I understand why Amorino is popular worldwide. It’s a bit on the pricier side, but absolutely worth trying.”

title: FIX Coffeebar – Creative Lattes & Cozy Montrose Vibes
description: FIX Coffeebar is a warm, intimate neighborhood café tucked into Montrose—full of wood textures, glowing bulb lights, and the soft hum of students and creatives typing away. author: Sara Loren
html:
FIX Coffeebar is a warm, intimate neighborhood café tucked into Montrose—full of wood textures, glowing bulb lights, and the soft hum of students and creatives typing away. Though compact, the space is thoughtfully arranged, with plenty of usable seating and a rotating menu of inventive, house-crafted lattes. FIX thrives on creativity, releasing seasonal flavors and even celebratory drinks like their birthday cake latte (only available in July). If you’re looking for a cozy, community-driven café with personality, this is the spot.


What to Order

  • Honey Lavender Latte – Balanced, fragrant, creamy, and beautifully blended. 

  • Seasonal Latte Special – Rotating flavors tied to holidays and seasonal inspiration. 

  • Breakfast Taco or Sandwich – Simple, warm pairings to enjoy with their specialty drinks.


Review

Sara I. (Dec 29, 2018):

“I finally had the chance to try out Fix Coffeebar on a rainy mid-week afternoon. Parking is far too few in this part of town—the plaza was packed, and I ended up parking on a corner street, mud everywhere. But alas, I made my trek into the world of caffeine.


Upon entering, you’ll notice the unique layout: warm string lights, wood elements, and a large patterned wood frame against the main wall. Though small, the café is arranged well, with plenty of tables and space for all the students and laptop workers buzzing around on a mid-afternoon weekday.


I was eager to try the birthday cake latte, only to learn it’s only served in July for the café’s anniversary—perfect for my own birthday month anyway. Instead, I opted for the honey lavender latte and was incredibly impressed. I expected the lavender to overpower the honey, but instead they danced together and created a wonderful taste. Creamy, smooth, and not acidic at all.


A few other unique flavors were listed for the winter season. FIX seems to rotate and experiment throughout the year, crafting creative flavor profiles. You can tell this place is passionate about the art + science behind their beverages. Warm, chill vibes, and a friendly barista made the visit even better. Looking forward to returning.”



Category: Coffee & Tea, Sandwiches, Tacos 

Location: Montrose, Houston, TX 


Tags: FIX Coffeebar Houston, lavender latte Houston, Montrose coffee shops, seasonal lattes Houston, study cafés Houston, specialty coffee Montrose

title: Sephora at Kohl’s – A Convenient, Calm Beauty Stop in Westchase
description: The Sephora at Kohl’s in Westchase brings a refreshing twist to the traditional Sephora experience—calmer, cleaner, less crowded, and wonderfully convenient. Open since June 2023, this compact yet well-stocked beauty kiosk sits just inside the Kohl’s entrance, making it an easy stop during a quick errand run or a dedicated beauty shopping trip.Despite its smaller footprint, the selection mirrors that of larger Sephora locations: fragrances, lotions, makeup, skincare, and gift items all line the
author: Sara Loren
html:
The Sephora at Kohl’s in Westchase brings a refreshing twist to the traditional Sephora experience—calmer, cleaner, less crowded, and wonderfully convenient. Open since June 2023, this compact yet well-stocked beauty kiosk sits just inside the Kohl’s entrance, making it an easy stop during a quick errand run or a dedicated beauty shopping trip.


Despite its smaller footprint, the selection mirrors that of larger Sephora locations: fragrances, lotions, makeup, skincare, and gift items all line the shelves. The space feels airy and relaxed, offering the rare pleasure of browsing beauty products without the usual bustle, perfume cloud, or shoulder bumping typical of busier stores.

Customer service shines here, with friendly greetings, helpful answers, and smooth checkout experiences—including the use of account points and seasonal discounts. Nestled in a growing and vibrant part of West Houston, this location adds a modern, accessible beauty option to the neighborhood.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Calm, crowd-free shopping environment

  • Surprisingly large selection for a kiosk-style setup

  • Quick in-and-out convenience

  • Friendly and attentive customer service

  • Easy rewards redemption & holiday promotions

  • Located in a thriving Westchase retail corridor


Review

Sara I. (Dec 9, 2023 – First to Review):

 “So this is a new location of Sephora and they have been open since June 2023. Walk inside Kohl's and you'll spot Sephora's fairly decent sized kiosk store to the left side of the store. I can't remember the last time I visited a Kohl's location, but this made for a good walk and fun visit.


I actually like this location! It's smaller compared to their regular stores yet they pretty much have every item that you would find at regular Sephora stores. Lotions, fragrances and gift items? Check. You'll find it here. This location is less crowded and you'll find what you need within a minute. There aren't people bumping or pushing against you at their other stuffy locations that reek of perfume and blush.


Customer service was great, I was greeted upon visiting and had all my questions answered. Found what that I was looking for and that's all there is to it. I was able to use my account points and they also gave a discount with it being the holidays. Perfect! Although the Galleria location is much closer to me, I can definitely see myself revisiting this one more often.


This new location of Sephora is in one of my favorite parts of town. I love how new businesses continue to develop within this west Houston urban neighborhood.


This business location needs to be revamped with saying ‘now opened’ instead of ‘coming soon.’ You're welcome and enjoy. SYOY.”


Category: Cosmetics & Beauty Supply 

Location: Westchase, Houston 


Tags: Sephora at Kohl’s Houston, Westchase beauty stores, makeup shopping Houston, fragrance gifts Houston, Sephora kiosk review, holiday beauty shopping

title: Mazajj Organic Coffee – A Warm, Light-Filled Chai Haven in Galleria/Uptown
description: Mazajj Organic Coffee brings a refreshing global warmth to the Galleria/Uptown area, offering an inviting space filled with natural light, stylish décor, and some of the city’s most lovingly crafted chai. With a freshly opened storefront closer to Houston’s inner loop than their Katy location, this café has already become a neighborhood favorite for anyone seeking a cozy, cultural, and aromatic coffeehouse experience.The atmosphere blends modern elegance with international charm—sunlight pouring
author: Sara Loren
html:
Mazajj Organic Coffee brings a refreshing global warmth to the Galleria/Uptown area, offering an inviting space filled with natural light, stylish décor, and some of the city’s most lovingly crafted chai. With a freshly opened storefront closer to Houston’s inner loop than their Katy location, this café has already become a neighborhood favorite for anyone seeking a cozy, cultural, and aromatic coffeehouse experience.

The atmosphere blends modern elegance with international charm—sunlight pouring through large windows, warm hospitality from the staff, and ambient music that feels transportive. Whether you’re settling in for a quiet morning, an evening wind-down, or a meetup with friends, Mazajj’s ambiance is as memorable as its drinks.


Must-Try Items:

  • Adeni Chai (light, creamy & perfectly balanced; available by the cup or teapot)

  • Coffee selections made with quality beans

  • Desserts including viral Dubai-style chocolate & milk cakes

  • Complimentary treats during special events or openings


Reviews

Sara I. (Sep 17, 2024 – First to Review, ROTD Dec 22, 2024): 

“Absolutely wonderful interior, lots of indoor lighting as well as natural lighting pouring in through the windows. Great customer service and warm hospitality, thanks guys!


This Mazajj is a lot closer within the inner loop of Houston compared to their Katy location. Their Katy shoppe is just as lovely though, with similar interior deco and piping hot tea.


Choices for teas and beverages are plenty. Want coffee? They've got it. Want tea? They have different styles. My favorite being the Adeni chai. It's not too strong as other spots make it. A bit of a lighter and creamier flavor. I always opt for half sweet and it's perfect. You can get it by the cup or as a teapot. I love their teapot and glassware. Adorable and makes for a cozy morning or evening spent sipping on chai. Warm and exotic music playing in the background makes for such an international vibe. I'm loving how they're situated within the Galleria area. We really needed a spot for authentic chai and Mazajj delivers! They just had their grand opening 2 days ago & already got it down in terms of customer service. Thanks for the complimentary desserts today. So sweet.


Y'all, check out Mazajj and thank me later. Support local and support chai that's made from scratch with true warmth and passion. Try their desserts, viral Dubai chocolate and milk cakes. So good and so worth it. Welcome to the neighborhood!”



Category: Coffee & Tea 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston 


Tags: Mazajj Organic Coffee Houston, Adeni chai Houston, Galleria coffee shops, Middle Eastern cafés Texas, authentic chai Houston, Dubai desserts Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
Nails by Yen has evolved over the years into a reliably warm, clean, and friendly neighborhood salon. Known for its large massage-chair pedicure stations, vivid polish selection, and consistently tidy setup, it remains a local favorite for simple manicures, relaxing pedicures, and quick self-care appointments. Technicians are attentive, personable, and often remember returning clients—building a sense of familiarity that keeps many regulars coming back.


What to Expect

  • Comfortable massage-chair pedicure stations

  • Friendly technicians who remember regular clients

  • Clean, well-maintained salon environment

  • Good polish selection with bright, fresh colors

  • Appointment reminders and courtesy calls

  • Discounted basic manicures on select weekdays


Reviews

Sara I. (Dec 15, 2021):

 “Great service—it has improved over the years. Many of the nail technicians are friendly and will remember you if you visit often. Joanne and Audrey are always friendly and socialize with everyone. This spot has remained nice and clean over time, with plenty of comfortable pedicure seats. They’ll offer drinks if you ask; I typically go for a water bottle. They also have a vivid selection of nail polish that’s never stale. Convenient, courteous, and prompt—they’ll even call if you're running late. This place has been a family favorite for years. Until next time!”

Sara I. (Jul 21, 2016): 

“I came here about once a month and was made to feel like a stranger. Some customers received warm greetings while others didn’t, which was disappointing. I was never asked if I wanted water until I finally asked for it on a hot day. Nonetheless, the manicures and pedicures were consistent, especially on Mondays and Tuesdays when the basic manicure is discounted. I appreciated the clean polish look and occasional decorative nail art.”

Sara I. (May 15, 2016):

 “Great service. I often came on Mondays or Tuesdays for their $10 basic manicure—it always got the job done. If you paid in cash, you received a small discount. Clean, reliable, and relaxing. The deluxe pedicure was lovely and pampering.”


Category: Nail Salons, Skin Care, Waxing

author: Sara Loren
html:
Arnaldo Richard’s Picos has long been a recognizable name in Houston’s Mexican and Tex-Mex dining scene, especially in the bustling Upper Kirby neighborhood. Known for its vibrant atmosphere, expansive menu, and decades-long presence in the community, Picos draws crowds throughout the week. But even longstanding favorites can have off days—and this visit, unfortunately, leaned that way.


Between slow service, missing items, and dishes that didn’t quite shine, the dining experience felt uneven. While the restaurant’s lively ambiance is usually part of its charm, the noise level paired with spotty service made the evening more stressful than enjoyable, especially with a toddler in tow. With Picos closing soon, this visit may not have showcased the restaurant’s best, but it captures an honest moment from a longtime Houston diner.


What to Know:

  • Popular for Mexican & Tex-Mex staples

  • Service can be hit or miss depending on timing

  • HRW (Houston Restaurant Weeks) menu experience may vary

  • Ceviche and enchiladas were heavier and less refined than expected

  • Desserts may be served small or delayed during busy hours


Reviews

Sara I. (Aug 22, 2025):

 “I thought the food here was just okay.


The service was incredibly spotty and it was incredibly loud inside the restaurant. I had to flag down the waiter a few times and the food came out pretty slowly. A group of us ordered from the Houston Restaurant Week menu and never even received our dessert. I had to ask for a to-go box for the dessert by that time as it was quite late and I had my toddler with me. How can a waiter forget to bring dessert when it's connected to the HRW menu?


Anyway, everything was just okay. The dessert came out as a tiny morsel in the to-go box. The food items we shared were just okay, such as the ceviche being rubbery and the enchiladas were quite heavy. This was my first experience at Pico's and probably my last as they are shutting down anyway. Maybe this spot is better earlier in the day or something, but I wasn't truly that impressed. Sorry.”



Category: Mexican, Tex-Mex, Breakfast & Brunch 

Location: Upper Kirby, Houston 


Tags: Picos Houston review, Tex-Mex Upper Kirby, Houston Restaurant Weeks experiences, Mexican restaurants Houston, family dining Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
Bering’s is the kind of Houston staple that makes browsing feel like an adventure—warm, whimsical, and full of treasures across every aisle. Whether you're hunting for a new cookbook, upgrading your kitchen tools, or discovering seasonal décor, this beloved shop always surprises with its thoughtfully curated offerings. Autumn brings an extra layer of charm, with golden hues filling the displays and cozy kitchen items begging to be taken home.


From culinary essentials to handmade chocolates, from stationery walls to playful in-store characters (yes, including their famous green parrot!), Bering’s blends practical shopping with feel-good nostalgia. It's a delightful spot to wander with family, snag last-minute gifts, or sip coffee while exploring new finds. With frequent deals and weekend tasting samples, there’s always something new to enjoy.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Beautiful selections of cookbooks, kitchenware, and seasonal décor

  • Handmade chocolates, biscotti, and local coffee

  • Family-friendly atmosphere with an adorable in-store parrot

  • A wide range of gifts—from stationery to culinary equipment

  • Weekend food samples and engaging displays


Reviews

Sara I. (Aug 30, 2025):

“I stumbled upon a potato cookbook at Berings which will be perfect for bébé and I. Gotta love a good and hearty potato recipe, especially with cozy autumn around the corner.


The colorful wall of cookbooks is such a delight. To be fair, I visited today in hopes of finding a spicy salsas & moles cookbook, which I found on their website. But it was nowhere to be found within the brick and mortar shoppe. Alas, we settled for the savory potato book.


The autumnal kitchen aprons piqued my attention and I may revisit pretty soon. Everything is becoming gold and orange within the shoppe.


The large green parrot at the shoppe is quite amusing and adorable. We love interacting with him.


It's always fun to visit Bering's, they have something for everyone. They often have deals as well, talk about sweet! Oh and don't forget the coffee and chocolates. They have handmade chocolates, biscotti and local coffee. The culinary equipment here is quite nice, whether you're looking for a new teapot, knife set or mugs, bowls. They often have food sample displays during the weekend as well, in particular, Saturday morning. Come check it out!”



Category: Cards & Stationery, Furniture Stores, Hardware Stores

Location: Houston, TX

author: Sara Loren
html:
Discover Grady Park, a tranquil urban retreat in Houston’s vibrant Galleria/Uptown area, perfect for families and outdoor enthusiasts. Located on Yorktown Drive, this hidden gem offers a peaceful escape from the city’s bustle, with a scenic walking trail ideal for jogs, strolls, or dog walks (leash up, please!). The kid-friendly playground, complete with swings, slides, and climbing features, is a hotspot for little adventurers, while the tennis court beckons players for a quick match.


Plan a sunny afternoon picnic, snap Instagram-worthy shots of the greenery, or organize a casual family gathering—Grady Park’s laid-back vibe suits all. For the best experience, visit during daylight to enjoy the full charm of this Houston park. It’s a must-visit for locals seeking free outdoor activities in the heart of the city.


Activities to Enjoy:

  • Jog or walk the scenic trail for a refreshing workout.

  • Let kids explore the playground’s slides and swings.

  • Play a friendly tennis match on the court.

  • Host a picnic or photo session with Houston’s skyline as a backdrop.


Reviews

Sara I. (March 15, 2025):

“This is a chill, quiet and clean park within the inner loop/galleria area. An urban park situated on Yorktown Drive. A bit of a green nature escape among the concrete plazas of inner loop Houston. Decent walking trail, kids play area and tennis court. I have mixed feelings about this park at evening though and it’s rather dark at evening. Barely any lights at that time. Be cautious at your own risk and visit the park during daylight hours. It’s non discrete and far from pretentious. A good place to get in fresh air and a few laps around the trail. The play area for kids isn’t that big, but it’s fun enough with various trinkets and slides. The swings for the kiddos and babies are available as well. Lots of joy and a spot to take photos. Grady Park is chill, I’ve taken the bebe here and we’ve captured some fun moments of his first experience on the swings and slides. Be careful with your possessions while visiting any park and as I mentioned, visit during daylight hours. Toodles!”



Category: Parks, Playgrounds

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
Embark on a culinary journey at Acacia Food Mart, a Fondren Southwest gem bringing authentic Turkish and international flavors to Houston. This cozy international grocery store is a haven for food lovers, offering shelves stocked with aromatic spices, premium lentils, European chocolates, and Turkish teas. The on-site bakery steals the show, serving up fresh breads and melt-in-your-mouth baklava that make every visit a treat.

Explore the unique home goods section for Turkish tea cups or artisanal soaps, perfect for gifts or home décor. With plenty of parking and extended hours, Acacia is a top pick for Houston foodies planning a global-inspired meal. Visit this Houston market to elevate your cooking game and savor the tastes of Turkey.


Activities to Enjoy:

  • Shop for Turkish spices and fresh bakery items.

  • Discover unique home goods for gifting.

  • Plan a Turkish-themed dinner party with authentic ingredients.

  • Treat yourself to baklava or fresh bread on-site.


Reviews

Sara I. (March 6, 2025):

 “I enjoyed my time at Acacia food market this week. This market is a little small, but you'll be sure to find most things here that are Turkish/European/International. I love their packaged chocolates, dried spices, lentils/rice,, fresh baklava and fresh baked bread. I grew up eating most of these items, so I love both their fresh items from their bakery as well as their packaged items from their store shelves. Customer service is little to none, it might be language barrier related, but I'm not bothered by it. When I visit this market, I know what I want. As a person that enjoys international cooking, I enjoy walking through various aisles. They have a lovely little bakery in the back corner of their market as mentioned. You can smell the fresh bread that is baked on a daily basis. They have quite a few dessert options, but my favorite will always be their baklava. They also have a "home" section with glassware,, Turkish tea cups, storage containers, soaps, etc. I found some baby products here as well!


I enjoyed the bakery bread when I got home and paired it with my homemade Turkish red lentil soup. So nourishing! Cozy and comfort at its finest.


Although a relatively small shoppe, they have quite a few things here. Parking is plenty, and they have long store hours as well. Come check this spot out!”


Category: International Grocery, Meat Shops 

Location: Fondren Southwest, Houston


Tags: Turkish Grocery, International Foods, Houston Food Markets, Baklava

author: Sara Loren
html:
Craving authentic Chinese food in Houston’s Galleria? Dumplings & Noodles by Cooking Girl is a lively destination for noodle lovers and dumpling fans. This modern eatery, part of the beloved Cooking Girl chain, serves up steaming bowls of noodles, flavorful dumplings, and budget-friendly lunch specials that include free veggie egg rolls and hot and sour soup. From savory beef and broccoli to spicy pepper dishes, the menu caters to all palates.


Located in the heart of Galleria/Uptown, it’s perfect for a quick lunch break or a post-shopping meal. Pair your dish with a refreshing boba tea for the ultimate Houston dining experience. With its welcoming vibe and prime location, this Chinese restaurant is a must-try for foodies exploring Houston’s culinary scene.


Top Picks:

  • Enjoy affordable lunch specials with free sides.

  • Sample dumplings or spicy noodle dishes.

  • Sip boba tea for a sweet treat.

  • Combine dining with Galleria shopping.


Reviews

Sara I. (January 22, 2025):

 “I wish I could've liked the food here but it was just okay. We ordered the fried chicken today as an appetizer and it literally came out as crumbs, almost "bottom of the bag" crumb type. It was like pecking with crumbs with a chopstick, terrible. A bad rendition of Taiwanese style popcorn chicken. The lunch portions are decent but the food is just okay as mentioned. I liked the crispy veggie egg roll and the hot and sour soup was filling and warm. These were the items I enjoyed within our lunch hangout. These 2 items are complimentary when you dine in for their lunch menu deal. The beef and broccoli lunch choice was decent. It was fresh and warm, not that salty. Paired well with steamed rice. I appreciated the flavors but I would try something else next time around from their main menu item. I like food on the spicier side and would try one of their pepper based items. I have had their hot diving fish in the past and it's decent, similar to other Cooking Girl locations. But, this location is a little different with the emphasis of "dumplings and noodles"


Steamed beef and onion dumplings are good, I suggest that item if you're looking to dine-in.


I have to admit that I like the food at their other locations better. I have always enjoyed dining in or getting "to-go" from most Cooking Girl locations. But this location is subpar at best. They do have nice and cordial customer service and it's conveniently located within the Houston Galleria area. This part of town doesn't have too many options for this style of cuisine. I hope y'all can improve in some aspects. Their iced milk tea/boba drinks look good. Perhaps I'll revisit and grab an go' a drink and a small item.


Toodles and see ya next time!”


Category: Chinese 

Location: Galleria/Uptown, Houston 


Tags: Chinese Restaurants, Dumplings Houston, Galleria Dining, Boba Tea

  • Ice cream and refreshing fruit drinks

  • Mexican-style snacks like elotes and nachos

Reviews

Sara I. (July 2, 2025):

"I like this spot and it's pretty refreshing like it's namesake. They have soo many colorful fruit flavors here and various ice cream as well. Wanting something savory or salty?..Refresqueria has that as well! Pickles, corn in a cup, nachos, and all that jazz. I have tried the mangonada here and it's one of my favorites. They add plenty of toppings and chamoy as well. I love the addition of gummy candies and you can top your drinks with other blended fruits as well. Honestly y'all, this is a good corner spot for some cravings. This Refresqueria spot feels like home in Rice Village. Before that, this corner used to be a coffee shoppe but I am so glad that Refresqueria is here. It is colorful, vibrant and definitely brings joy on these hot summer days. I recommend trying it during these stretched heated days that call for a juicy and fruity blended beverage. It's a great hangout spot to bring family and friends. They have a few games as well as a retro arcade game as well. Anyway, until next time!"

html:
Step into the sugary charm of Milk Mustache, a whimsical cookie shop tucked into Fountain View in the Galleria/Uptown area. This isn’t your average dessert spot—it’s a full sensory experience. As soon as you walk in, you’re wrapped in the warm aroma of buttery dough and nostalgic sweetness. With its colorful, cozy atmosphere and standout service, Milk Mustache is a must-visit for any dessert lover in Houston.


Their cookies are a true craft—crispy on the edges, gooey in the middle, and craggy in the best way possible. This local gem rotates in fresh flavors throughout the year, keeping things exciting with options like soft serve and dessert drinks. It’s a perfect stop for a quick treat, a post-lunch indulgence, or a sugary gift for a loved one.


Must-Try Treats:

  • Warm, gooey cookies with rotating seasonal flavors

  • Sweet dessert beverages and soft serve ice cream

  • A cute, Instagram-worthy interior


Review:

Sara I. (July 2, 2025):

“Yummy cookies galore.


I have always liked this sweet gem of a spot. When you walk into milk mustache, you smell all things butter and sweetness. The aroma wafts in the cute little shoppe. It is every so colorful, cute and whimsical in here. I love this cozy yet nonchalant cookie shoppe right on fountain view. Milk Mustache honestly has some of the best cookies in the city. That says a lot, cause' we've got quite a few cookie/dessert spots in the city. But I'm picky and I truly believe these are some of the best cookies I've had in Houston. They are warm, crispy and yet gooey as well. They have that classic texture and flavor that a cookie should measure up to.. and they are crag like. I love how this spot has a few new flavors throughout the year and they also have dessert beverages and soft serve as well. Service is always nice and prompt. The dessert's here are quite sweet but full of flavor, which keeps me revisiting every now and then. Try it for yourself, you'll be in for a treat. Nothing dry and nothing boring about these cute cookies. Until next time!”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Golem’s Gate in Stafford feels like stepping into a pocket-sized fantasy realm—warm, welcoming, and brimming with imagination. This independently owned mom-and-pop shop is tucked into a quiet corner of town, but inside, it’s vibrant with creativity. Owners Tama and Jason bring heart to the space, offering friendly guidance, recommendations, and an infectious passion for all things tabletop and geekdom.


The shop is stocked with everything a gamer or collector could want: books, miniatures, board games, gaming accessories, plushies, and nostalgic treasures. Whether you're a seasoned Dungeons & Dragons player or a newcomer curious about the world of tabletop adventures, Golem’s Gate invites you to explore, learn, and play. Renting board games is encouraged, and the community atmosphere makes it easy to settle in with friends for a fun escape from the everyday.


Tuesday evening D&D nights bring the shop to life, blending 80s nostalgia with the modern revival of role-playing games. Costumes are welcome, creativity is celebrated, and seasonal holidays—especially Halloween—add extra charm to this already magical spot. Golem’s Gate is the kind of store where phones are forgotten, imaginations take over, and everyone gets to play a character of their choosing.


Why You’ll Love It:

  • Friendly owners who make newcomers feel at home

  • Wide selection of games, miniatures, accessories & collectibles

  • Board game rentals for fun hangouts

  • Weekly Dungeons & Dragons nights

  • Nostalgic, fantasy-inspired atmosphere

  • A great place to unplug, dress up & let imagination roam


Review

Sara I. (Oct 30, 2024): 

“This is such a neat little mom and pop game store that is tucked in a quiet and cozy little part of town. The store owners, Tama and Jason are friendly, they will be quick to show you around & answer any questions you may have. They have a variety of books, miniatures, plushies and board games. Many gaming accessories for those that are into that type of stuff. Very fantasy like spot that will buzz the imagination of any that walks into the shoppe. You can also rent a board game and play with friends. On Tuesday evenings, the community hosts dungeons and dragons board game nights. A popular game from the 80s that has definitely had a revamp and has its own return into the world of board games.


This is a fun little store where you can really be yourself and tap into your imagination. Dressing up in costumes is allowed and you can play the role of any character that comes to mind. Halloween is probably such a fun little time to explore Golems Gate, as well as any other seasonal holiday. Bring in your friends to this store and have fun! The more the merrier. This spot is a little nostalgic for those that love anything retro as well. A place where you can chat it up, put your phones away and do something a bit different. How's that for nostalgia? Cheers!”

title: La Argentina Gelato & Coffee – A Quiet Spot with Room to Grow
description: [PERMANENTLY CLOSED - Store No Longer Operating] La Argentina Gelato & Coffee is a small, tucked-away spot offering South American–style gelato and baked treats. author: Sara Loren
html:
[PERMANENTLY CLOSED - Store No Longer Operating]


La Argentina Gelato & Coffee is a small, tucked-away spot offering South American–style gelato and baked treats. While its reputation has generated quite a bit of buzz, this particular visit left room for improvement. Hidden in a low-traffic corner and offering only a handful of flavors, the experience felt more subdued than the hype suggested.


Customer service presented some communication challenges, making it difficult to ask questions or explore the menu fully. The gelato itself was just okay, and the alfajores—typically known for their soft, tender crumb and creamy dulce de leche—fell short. Hard texture, brittle cookie, and a firm filling made the treat surprisingly disappointing. Still, gelato quality can vary by time of day, and the mid-evening visit may not have captured the shop at its best.


With South American gelato differing in style from Italian versions, and with many positive notes about their coffee, a future visit may offer a better impression. Frozen treat lovers may still find a reason to return and give the flavors another chance, especially alongside a well-reviewed espresso or latte.


What to Try (Next Visit):

  • A fresh batch of gelato earlier in the day

  • Coffee drinks, which receive strong praise

  • Skip the cookies; focus on frozen treats


Review

Sara I. (Aug 11, 2023):

 “I thought this spot was just alright. What a hype. Location wise, it is not the easiest to spot, tucked away in a corner of an area that is typically not frequented.


In regards to customer service? It was hard to navigate the conversation due to language barriers. I passionately had a few questions in mind.. but was not able to clearly articulate them due to said obstacle.

Bit of a small spot with few gelato flavors to pick from.. The gelato was just okay... even worse... the alfajores was downright awful. Hard in taste.. and the dulce de leche interior was hard as well. When I imagine alfajores.. it is tender, melt in your mouth, with the dulce de leche being of a very sweet and creamy interior. This one fell short of how the cookie should crumble.. or rather it just disintegrated into dust. Shortbread cookies made with love are awesome.. this one wasn't.


Perhaps it was the time of day we visited.. towards mid-evening. I'll have to revisit in the future certainly.. as I'm a huge fan of frozen treats.. especially gelato. I also understand that South American gelato is different than Italian style gelato.. as I've tried it before through my travels overseas. I want to give their gelato one more try next time around and perhaps pair it with their coffee which seems to get mad reviews. I would stay away from the cookies though and focus on their frozen treats. Here's hoping our next encounter will be a sweeter one.”

Location: Houston, TX

title: Slim Chickens – A Pearland Visit with Hits, Misses & a Lot of Sauce Potential
description: Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston—often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. This Pearland visit, however, delivered a mixed experience: a few standout bites, a few letdowns, and a whole lot of room for improvement. Unfortunately, the rest of the plate did
author: Sara Loren
html:
Slim Chickens is one of those spots you see scattered across Houston—often enticing enough to spark curiosity and high expectations. This Pearland visit, however, delivered a mixed experience: a few standout bites, a few letdowns, and a whole lot of room for improvement. While the concept is promising and the menu broad, not everything hit the mark this time around.


The fried mushrooms were the star of the meal—crispy, warm, and full of satisfying texture. Unfortunately, the rest of the plate didn’t follow suit. The tenders lacked crispness, the fries leaned soft rather than crunchy, and the Texas toast was serviceable but unremarkable. The much-hyped Slims sauce, said to resemble Cane’s, leaned more toward creamy tomato soup than tangy dipping bliss, making it a surprise mismatch for the meal. To top it off, the ranch—requested as a backup savior—never made it into the to-go bag.


Still, Slim Chickens offers a wide selection of sandwiches, wraps, and comforting desserts, leaving the door open for a possible revisit at another location. And for dessert lovers, the pudding jars and cheesecake cups may be the hidden gems worth exploring—especially on a hot Texas day.


Hit or Miss Menu Notes: 

Hits:

  • Fried mushrooms — warm, crispy & delicious

Misses:

  • Soft fries

  • Not-so-crispy tenders

  • Slims sauce (unexpectedly tomato-forward)

  • Missing ranch from the order

Worth Trying Next Time:

  • Sandwiches & wraps

  • Pudding jars & cheesecake desserts


Reviews

Sara I. (Jul 18, 2023):

 “Hmm Slim Chickens! More like the bare bones of it. A place that I had high expectations for, but to be honest, those expectations fell flat upon first sight and bite.


I was excited to try this spot and have noticed it in different parts of Houston but happened to be out in the city of Pears and found it out of happenstance. Twas' evening time and the hunger pangs began for a snack. Something not too heavy, but not too light. My initial thoughts were to visit Canes because I was craving their sauce and tenders, but didn't know which side of Pearland it was at. Slims popped up during my excursion and I thought.. well why not? I've seen this spot before so let’s give it a shot.


Ordered their simple meal of tenders that came with fries and texas toast. Also ordered their fried mushrooms as well. The fried mushrooms were bomb! Incredibly warm and crispy. They had good texture and taste. I wish I could say the same for the rest of my meal, but everything else was OK (fries and tenders). The tenders weren't that crispy, maybe because of all that buttermilk batter? They were also a bit small. Fries weren't crispy, mostly soft. Texas toast was buttery and garlicky, it was average in taste.


I was excited to try their Slims sauce, which I was told was similar to Canes. At least that's what the drive thru staff said. With excitement I asked for 2 orders of their Slims sauce. To my surprise, it did not taste anything similar to Canes sauce. Instead it was very creamy and tomato flavored in taste. Almost like a cream of tomato soup which did not pair well with any of the items that were ordered. I also asked for ranch sauce as well which they forgot to add to my order when I left - that would have been the saving grace to those tenders.


With a plethora of sauce that this place has to offer, I'm sure that I would have a better experience with a different flavor profile. But will I be back? I'm not too sure. I do like how they offer other items on their menu such as sandwiches and wraps. Might visit another location within the Houston area. I was just left unimpressed. Thankfully the meal wasn't as salty or aggressively fried in flavor as other fast foods spots. Slim' ranking for this spot. But might revisit if having a hankering for some tenders. Unless I'm cravin' for another kinda sauce. Until next time.


PS - they are serving up cheesecake desserts & various pudding jar desserts... perhaps something sweeter and cooling in this heat would be nice.”


Category: Southern, Comfort Food, American

Location: Pearland, TX 


Tags: Slim Chickens review, Pearland comfort food, chicken tenders Houston area, fried mushrooms Pearland, fast casual Southern food, sauce lovers Houston

author: Sara Loren
html:
[PERMANENTLY CLOSED - Store No Longer Operating] 


A warm summer evening set the stage for an intimate and unforgettable chef’s table experience at Yi Peng Thai Dining in CityCentre. What many expected to be a traditional Thai dinner transformed into a sophisticated parade of artisanal small plates, each crafted with bold flavors, rich textures, and a sense of culinary storytelling.


From the moment the dishes began arriving—one after another in elegant progression—the night took on an electric, joyful energy. The short ribs and crispy chicken were standout favorites, decadent without being heavy, balanced by refreshing sips of sweet Thai tea and fresh coconut water lightly iced with slivers of coconut meat.

Chef Jett brought charisma and passion to the table, engaging guests with lively conversation and insights into Thai cuisine. Meeting him, along with his wife and the talented culinary team, added a personal touch to an already immersive dining experience. Their hospitality, warmth, and cultural pride elevated the evening into something far more meaningful than a simple dinner.


The event sparked wanderlust—visions of Thailand, fragrant penang curry, and kaffir lime leaves drifting through the mind long after dessert. Equally delightful was reconnecting with longtime friends and celebrating the evolution of Houston’s food community, where creative and culturally rich gatherings continue to flourish.


Event Highlights:

  • Artisanal Thai small plates

  • Slow-braised short ribs

  • Crispy chicken with bold seasoning

  • Sweet Thai tea & fresh chilled coconut water

  • Intimate conversations with Chef Jett

  • A lively, cozy summer-night atmosphere


Review

Sara I. (Aug 18, 2022):

“Well. What can I say? All my favorite platinum folk already wrote essays upon essays about our grandeur Thai inspired evening in City Centre. It was a cosy summer night as we noshed upon food that was as big & bold with flavor, as our conversations were.


I adored the bold and spunky energy at the table—full of laughter, honesty, and depth. I kept thinking we would eat typical Thai cuisine that night. But that was far from our reality… we were gifted with artisanal small plated meals that were decadent yet rich in taste. My favorites were the short ribs and crispy chicken. Thai tea was quite sweet yet refreshing in between savory meals. Their fresh coconut water was great as well. A bit of coconut meat and lightly iced, it was perfect in this summer season.


Chef Jett was enthusiastic, energetic and fun to speak with. His name is quite huge in this city and it was lovely to finally meet him. His wife and the rest of the culinary team were friendly and informative as well. Thanks to the Thai cultural ministry in their initiative to feed us and tickle our taste-buds & minds.


Now I have a strong longing and impulse to visit Thailand and nosh on penang curry that's sprinkled with just the right amount of kaffir lime leaves. Aside from my wanderlust daydream, I had a great evening catching up with old-school friends. With summer finally ending (I think), it was a great initiative catching up and learning about prospective events and the growth of the community.


Much has changed in the past decade... nostalgia of days gone by… but so much growth and fun still ahead. Cheers!


PS — Thanks for the lippy balm, mints, and other cute little gifts. The remembrance of a fun night will linger longer than the taste of those mints.”

Teapresso Bar in Sugar Land brings a Hawaiian-inspired twist to the local café scene, offering Kona coffee, milk teas, hot beverages, and customizable drinks with organic coffee beans—something not easily found in this part of town. With warm wooden tables, bright interiors, and plenty of seating, it’s a convenient place to study, work, or wind down with a drink.


However, the experience can be hit-or-miss. Once known for friendly service and quality drinks, this location has seen a noticeable decline in customer care, atmosphere, and consistency. Prices have crept up, and the staff’s demeanor has grown increasingly aloof. Still, for locals seeking real milk (not powdered creamer) and solid coffee options, Teapresso Bar remains one of the few alternatives in Sugar Land.


The café continues to shine in its cleanliness, available seating, and steady drink lineup. But with a little more warmth and attentiveness, it could easily return to its former charm—especially in a city craving more unique coffee and tea destinations.


What to Order:

  • Organic coffee beverages

  • Tapioca drinks & milk teas

  • Kona coffee specialties

  • Light snacks & hot drinks

Atmosphere Notes:

  • Bright, clean interior

  • Board games & seating for laptops/work

  • Can get loud during drink preparation


Review

Sara I. (Jan 11, 2023): 

“This spot was unusually warm today and the service was mediocre at best; which seems to be the case lately. I've always liked Teapresso and really dig the location out in the Heights.. (if it's still around). But this location in the heart of Sugar Land could do way better. They were great when they first started out.. which was about 4 years ago. Since then the service has gone downhill and the drinks are steep in price.


The young lady at the front never smiles and seems to be irritated at any cost. Nonetheless, some of the drinks are still okay and it's one of the few spots where you can actually get a decent cup of coffee in Sugar Land. Simply because you have an option for choosing organic coffee beans and actual milk in your drinks. I always steer clear from non-dairy creamer and crap coffee.


I appreciate the fact that we have a Hawaiian style cafe in town that specializes in tapioca drinks, Kona coffee and a few other items. They have snacks as well as a few hot beverages. Plenty of seating with warm wooden tables and board games as well. It's a decent spot to get some work done or work on anything on your laptop. It can get loud at times because they're obviously making drinks in the corner.


All in all, it's a good spot in the area, especially with limited coffee choices (c'mon Sugar Land!). A bit bleak at times.. hoping they can regain their charm. Plus side? Always clean and bright inside.”

author: Sara Loren
html:
Zoa Moroccan Kitchen has built a name for itself across Houston with fast-casual Moroccan bowls, customizable toppings, and comforting warm flavors. With multiple locations around the city, it’s become a convenient go-to for lunch or dinner. However, experiences can vary—and this visit to the Bellaire location offered a noticeably different impression from others.


While the flavors remained solid—warm spices, tender meats, and enjoyable toppings—the portions at this location felt surprisingly skimpy for the price. The compact, grab-and-go setup and tight parking added to the sense that the visit didn’t quite measure up to the consistency of other Zoa kitchens. For two bowls, one bread, and a green tea totaling around $30, the value simply didn't match the experience, leaving diners still hungry and unsatisfied.


What to Know Before Visiting:

  • Portions at this location run small for the price

  • Food quality is good, but less impressive than other Zoa locations

  • Limited parking & small interior leaning toward takeout

  • Meats are tender; toppings flavorful

  • Moroccan green tea is delicious but very sweet


Reviews

Sara I. (Feb 12, 2024): 

“This was the third Zoa Moroccan Kitchen location that I have visited within Houston. They have locations all around the city and are rather convenient for visiting over lunch or dinner.


So far with this location? Unimpressed and left much to be desired. This location is super skimpy with their portions and the price point is heavy. For two bowls, 1 bread and 1 green tea, you'll shell out about $30 and leave feeling a bit underwhelmed. Not sure why they are so skimpy with their portions and their service. Food was good, warm and flavorful, but I've had better at their other locations.


This location is quite small and grab and go style as well. Parking is a bit small and limited and as mentioned, this location is smaller than the other ones that I have visited. With the food: The meats were tender and their toppings were decent. Unfortunately, I may never revisit ever again due to their lack of decent portions of their bowls and the overall presentation of their meals. I'm already hungry after writing this review and I was just visiting with their location not that long ago - LOL. Their super sweet Moroccan green tea is great, but honestly, I can make that at home (Atay Bi Nana).


We don't have that many Moroccan food choices in Houston, I wish Zoa could do a bit better. Probably won't revisit this location ever again as mentioned. Until next time!”

author: Sara Loren
html:
[PERMANENTLY CLOSED - Store No Longer Operating]


Al Rabba World Food brings a wide-ranging, multicultural grocery experience to a quiet corner of Sugar Land. Housed in what was once a neighborhood Randall’s, the store spans a large footprint with sections that alternate between spacious minimalism and fully stocked aisles. The result is an unexpected little adventure—one where shelves of spices, teas, cookware, and imported goods meet a modern halal butcher and a broad produce selection.


Fresh herbs, vegetables, and fruit are easy to find here, and the halal meat section is well-organized, neatly packaged, and properly dated. Though tucked deep within New Territory, far from major roads, the market offers a welcome blend of South Asian ingredients, American staples, and a few charming kitchen items that make wandering the aisles surprisingly fun.


Must-Find Items

  • Fresh herbs, peppers, ginger

  • Halal meats packaged and dated securely

  • International pantry items

  • Culinary equipment & dainty teacups

  • Large bakery section (for future exploring!)


Review

Sara I. (Jun 20, 2020): 

“I’m not sure where the low ratings are coming from—I had a nice experience today. Yes, some parts of the store feel barren while others are fully packed, but honestly that made it a little adventurous to sift through everything.


They have a large bakery (which I didn’t explore) and a great selection of produce. The herbs, peppers, ginger—all fresh. I make ginger tea often, so finding good quality ginger was essential. The halal meat section was extensive as well, with everything packaged and dated properly.


This is a huge market, previously a Randall’s, so you still see touches of the old grocery layout alongside international items. I even spotted culinary equipment and delicate teacups that caught my eye.


Though it’s nestled deep inside New Territory and a bit out of the way, it’s refreshing to have a diverse, clean market in Sugar Land. I won’t frequent it often due to distance, but I’m glad it’s here.”


Category: Halal, Indian, Pakistani

author: Sara Loren
html:
Jang Guem Tofu & BBQ has long been a dependable Sugar Land spot for hearty Korean comfort food—piping hot tofu soups, sizzling bulgogi, and a spread of banchan to round out the experience. Over the years, the menu has shifted, and though many dishes remain flavorful and satisfying, service quality has noticeably declined, leaving loyal diners conflicted.


The tofu soups, while warm, fresh, and deeply comforting, have grown increasingly salty. The once-favorite kimchi dumplings—formerly crisp, clean, and made purely of kimchi—are no longer available, replaced by versions mixed with pork and presented with a dismissive explanation. Vegetarian dumplings now fall into the “just okay” category. Meanwhile, blaring music and cold, condescending service dampen the dining experience, especially when simple requests like banchan refills become a challenge.


Still, the restaurant has its strengths: bulgogi arrives sizzling on stone plates, portions remain generous, and certain dishes retain the flavors that longtime guests once loved. For those nearby, Jang Guem may still be a convenient go-to—but with hopes that the service and attention to detail return to the welcoming warmth it once offered.


What Stands Out (Good & Bad): Hits:

  • Flavorful tofu soups (though salty)

  • Piping hot bulgogi on stone iron platters

  • Generous portions

Misses:

  • Confrontational, dismissive service

  • Loud, disruptive music

  • Decline in dumpling quality

  • Difficult to request banchan refills


Review

Sara I. (Mar 30, 2023): 

“Decent food, terrible service. I've been dining here for years and the menu has gone through a few changes. I used to love their kimchi dumplings that were made purely out of kimchi and nothing else. They used to be crisp, warm and delightful. Back when the restaurant used to give a damn. I asked if I could order that and noticed it's no longer on the menu. They mentioned that it's always mixed with pork. Negative! Sure, maybe your new updated menu, but take a look at your menu from 3 years ago.


The waiter spoke with a cold and condescending attitude. I thought to myself, why argue with someone that has barely worked here for that long? Ordered the vegetarian dumplings instead. Mediocre.


Moving on. I ordered the usual tofu soups that I like getting from here. Sure their soups are good, but definitely on the salty side. With a condescending attitude, I bet I can't make an adjustment to any soup that I'm willing to order. Their banchan is just okay. Want a refill of your banchan? Good luck flagging down the waiter. Music is blaring loud and awfully obnoxious within a small dine-in restaurant.


Again, some of the food items are good here. Decent portions and their beef bulgogi is decent as well. Piping warm and fresh... crackling on stone iron sets... but damn... Nevermind the salt! Mind blown.”


Category: Korean, Barbeque, Asian Fusion 

Location: Sugar Land, Texas 


Tags: Jang Guem Sugar Land review, Korean tofu soup Houston area, bulgogi Sugar Land, Korean BBQ Houston suburbs, banchan review Houston, restaurant service experiences

author: Sara Loren
html:
Yomie’s Rice X Yogurt brings a unique concept to Chinatown with its lineup of creamy, rice-based and yogurt-based beverages. These drinks are mellow, smooth, and lightly sweet—ideal after a spicy meal or when you’re craving something cooling and indulgent. The menu is playful and creative, though first-time visitors may find the ordering experience a bit unclear. Flavors lean mild and gentle rather than tart or punchy, making this a spot best suited for those who enjoy softer yogurt profiles.


Must-Try Items

  • Yogurt & Oats Drink

  • Dragon Fruit Series (when fruit is in season)

  • Classic Rice Yogurt Blends

  • Low-sweetness customization options


Review

Sara I. (Feb 22, 2022): 

“Service was super awkward, cold, and dry—just like the cutting winds outside that night. The drinks were okay: simple yogurt-based beverages that were creamy and mellow. I prefer sharper, tangier yogurt flavors, almost Mediterranean style, and theirs reminded me more of an Australian yogurt—light without any real zest. The dragon fruit didn’t shine through the yogurt at all, maybe because it wasn’t in season.


I did enjoy the yogurt and oats drink, though I wished it had more flavor. It wasn’t too sweet, which I appreciated since I asked for reduced sweetness. I was curious if fruit could be added to the oat drink—definitely a missed opportunity! The menu wasn’t explained to me, adding to the awkwardness.


These cold yogurt drinks are great after a spicy meal; the lactic base totally cuts the acid reflux. I couldn’t finish my drink and refrigerated the rest, thinking it might turn into overnight oats. Nope—the yogurt separated and tasted unpleasant the next day. Oops! Will I return? Maybe. But the service really needs improvement.”

description: Tønsberg Brygge sits at the heart of Norway’s oldest town—a place steeped in Viking history, maritime heritage, and quiet Scandinavian charm.
